stages.title: Pallet Town, and the partner you cannot change
body: Read this before anything else. Wild Pokémon are not battled. They stand in the overworld, you walk into one, and a throwing screen opens — you aim a ball and that is the whole encounter. Everything downstream of that changes: there is no wild-battle experience, so catching is how your party levels, and the number of species you have caught is a hard gate on gifts, Secret Techniques and one entire Gym.

Oak stops you at the edge of Pallet, drags you into the tall grass, and a Pikachu jumps out of his bag and refuses to leave. It cannot be boxed, it cannot evolve into Raichu, and it will be one of your six for the rest of the run. Your rival is Trace — a mild, friendly rival rather than Blue — and because you are playing Let’s Go, Pikachu! he takes the Eevee, which becomes a Jolteon by the mid-game.

Your partner is not a normal Pikachu and you should stop thinking of it as one. The partner has its own inflated base stats — 45 / 80 / 50 / 75 / 60 / 120 against a wild Pikachu’s 35 / 55 / 40 / 50 / 50 / 90 — which makes it a genuine attacker with the highest Speed you will own until Mewtwo. It gets three exclusive moves from tutors in three Pokémon Centers, plus a free fifth move. Build around it; do not bench it.

Partner Pikachu’s base stats, and the gain over a wild Pikachu. Attack sits above Special Attack, which is why its best move is a physical one.

The Pokémon Box lives in your Bag. There is no PC, and no reason to ever keep a party slot free — open the Bag from anywhere, tap the Box, and move Pokémon in and out on the spot. Every “box it here / free a slot” instruction you remember from the older Kanto games is dead weight in this game.

body.where: Route 1 — 40%, and Route 2 at 30%
body.why: Catch several. You do not need a Fly carrier in this game — the partner learns Sky Dash — so Pidgey is here purely for the species count and the experience its captures pay out.

body.where: Routes 1, 2 and 22 — 20–30%
body.why: The same job as Pidgey, plus it is the Pokémon a girl in Cerulean wants for an Alolan Rattata. Catch two.

body.where: Route 1 — 30%, Route 2 at 20%
body.why: Let’s Go, Pikachu! exclusive — Eevee players get Bellsprout instead. This is your key into the Pewter Gym, which turns away first-time challengers who cannot show a Grass or Water Pokémon. Water does not exist yet, so Oddish is the answer.

body.where: Route 22 — 20%
body.why: Route 22 is the only early grass with either Nidoran. Take one of each for the Pokédex; the male line is the better attacker if you keep it.

body.where: Route 22 — 30%
body.why: Species count and a warm body for the sixth slot. Fearow is fine early and completely outclassed by the time you reach Celadon.

body.where: Route 2 — 15%
body.why: Route 2 south is the cheapest Bug pair in the game. Catch Caterpie and Weedle here so you do not have to hunt them in the forest next stage.

body: Species caught is a currency in this game, and the bills come due quickly. Ten species buys the Light Up Secret Technique on Route 2. Thirty buys a free Bulbasaur in Cerulean and the IV Judge on Route 11. Fifty buys a free Charmander on Route 24 and entry to the Fuchsia Gym. Sixty buys a free Squirtle in Vermilion. Throwing balls at every duplicate is not padding — duplicates are your experience, and each new species is a key.

Oak gives you Razz Berries, not Poké Balls. Feed one before you throw and the target stays still and is easier to catch; a berry is almost always worth more than a second ball. Buy balls in Viridian with the money the game keeps giving you.

body.where: From the Poké Mart clerk in Viridian, then walked back to Oak
body.why: Forced errand. It buys you the Pokédex, so catch on the way down and back rather than running it twice.

body.where: Viridian City — west side of town
Route 22 — southwest corner
Route 22 — hidden in a bush north of the eastern grass
Viridian City — from the sleeping man in the south-west
body.why: Needs Chop Down, so you cannot have it yet. Note the man and come back in stage 07; a guaranteed burn halves physical damage for the rest of the fight.

body.t: Follow Oak into the grass north of town and take the partner Pikachu.
body.sub: Scripted. It joins at level 5 and never leaves your party — it cannot be deposited in the Box and it cannot evolve.

body.t: Take the Potion from the PC in your bedroom before you go.
Catch Pidgey, Rattata and Oddish on the way north — several of each.
body.sub: Pidgey 40%, Rattata 30%, Oddish 30%. Duplicates are your only source of experience until you meet a trainer, so throw at everything.

body.t: Take the free Potion from the Poké Mart clerk and the Oak’s Parcel he hands you with it.
Walk the Parcel back to Oak for the Pokédex.
body.sub: The game forces the round trip. Catch on the way down as well as the way back — the species count you build here unlocks three free starters later.

body.t: Buy Poké Balls and Razz Berries before you go anywhere else.
body.sub: Twenty balls and a stack of Razz Berries. Berries matter more than balls: a fed target barely moves.

body.t: Take the hidden Antidote in the bush north of the eastern grass.
body.sub: One of the first hidden items in the game, and easy to walk past.

body.t: Note the sleeping man in the south-west of town and leave him.
body.sub: He is holding TM11 Will-O-Wisp behind a small tree. You come back for it in stage 07 with Chop Down.

body.t: Go west out of Viridian before you go north.
body.sub: Route 22 is the only early grass with Nidoran♀ and Nidoran♂, at 20% each. Two more species, two more keys.

body.t: Catch Nidoran♂, Nidoran♀ and Spearow, and pick up the Poké Balls in the south-west corner.
Beat Trace at the league gate.
body.sub: In Let’s Go, Pikachu! he leads a level-6 Eevee with Tackle and Growl, plus a level-3 Pidgey if you took the optional battle in Viridian. Zippy Zap is not yours yet; Thunder Shock is enough.

body.t: Now head north out of Viridian, into Viridian Forest.
body.sub: You should be leaving with roughly twenty species logged and everything in the party at level 8 or 9.

stages.title: Boulder Badge — Brock, and the gym that checks your bag
body: The Pewter Gym turns first-time challengers away at the door. The guide will not let you past unless you can show him a Grass or Water Pokémon. No Water exists yet, so this means an Oddish from Route 1 or 2, or the rare Bulbasaur in Viridian Forest. If you skipped Oddish, go back for one now — it is a 30% spawn one screen south.

The forest is a short maze full of Bug Catchers. Because wild Pokémon are visible, the only thing worth slowing down for is the pair of rare spawns: species that are not on the ordinary encounter table at all and appear with a flourish and a chime. In this forest that is Bulbasaur, and in Let’s Go, Pikachu! there is also a wild Butterfree at 1%.

body.where: Viridian Forest — rare spawn, no fixed table slot
body.why: Worth ten minutes of circling. It is the same Pokémon Cerulean gives you free at 30 species, so it is not urgent — but catching one here means you have your Grass body before the Pewter Gym door check and can start levelling it immediately.

body.where: Viridian Forest — 5%
body.why: A wild Pikachu is not your partner and is a completely ordinary Pokémon with ordinary stats. Catch one anyway: it is the species the Saffron trade wants, once evolved with a Thunder Stone, for an Alolan Raichu.

body.where: Viridian Forest — 1%, Let’s Go, Pikachu! only
body.why: Version exclusive. Eevee players see a 1% Beedrill here instead. A fully evolved catch at level 3–6 is free experience and a species you would otherwise have to grind Caterpie for.

body.where: Viridian Forest — 25%
body.why: Metapod at 7, Butterfree at 10. If you did not catch the wild Butterfree, raising one is the cheap way to the third entry in the line.

body.where: Viridian Forest — 24%
body.why: Kakuna at 7, Beedrill at 10. Log the line and move on; nothing in it earns a party slot.

body: Rare spawns are how Let’s Go hands out species that have no encounter slot — Bulbasaur here, Charmander on Routes 3 and 4, Squirtle on Routes 24 and 25. They appear roughly 1 in 100 spawns at a Catch Combo of zero, and a chain of 31 or more pushes that to 50%. If you want a specific one, chain the commonest thing on the route rather than wandering.

body.where: From Trace as you enter town
Behind the Pokémon Center
From the lady west of the museum, after minding her Slowpoke
From Brock
body.why: 70 power physical Normal with a flinch chance. Genuinely fine filler on anything physical until better TMs turn up.

body.where: From Blue outside the gym, after you beat Brock
Pewter Museum — employee area, behind a small tree
body.why: Needs Chop Down. You cannot take it yet. Come back in stage 07; it becomes Aerodactyl at the Cinnabar Lab.

body.name: Brock

team.note: Tackle. That is the entire moveset. It exists to be removed.
Headbutt, Bind, Rock Throw. 160 base Defense against a 45 Attack — it is a wall with no hammer.

plan: Lead your Oddish or Bulbasaur. Absorb and Vine Whip are both 2× into Rock/Ground, and neither of Brock’s Pokémon can meaningfully hurt a Grass type back.

Your Pikachu learns Double Kick at level 9 — Fighting, 30 power, and it hits twice, which means it rolls through Onix’s enormous Defense far better than the raw number suggests. Have it before you walk in.

Electric does literally nothing here. Both of Brock’s Pokémon are part Ground, so Thunder Shock is a zero. This is the one gym where your partner’s STAB is dead weight and its Fighting move is the whole point.
Onix’s Bind chips you for 4–5 turns and stops you switching. If you are winning slowly, heal before it locks you in rather than after.
Do not bother with a Rock or Ground answer of your own. Brock is a level check you have already passed.
body.reward: TM01 Headbutt, the Boulder Badge, and obedience from traded Pokémon up to level 20. Badges do not boost your stats in this game — that was Generation I. All a badge does here is raise the obedience ceiling.

body: Badges buy obedience and nothing else. No Attack boost, no Defense boost, and no field moves: the Secret Techniques are taught by NPCs, not unlocked by badges. Obedience is set by how many badges you hold, not which ones — 1 → level 20, 2 → 30, 3 → 40, 4 → 50, 5 → 60, 6 → 70, 7 → 80, 8 → no limit — and it only ever applies to Pokémon you did not catch yourself.

body.t: Circle the forest for the Bulbasaur rare spawn before you leave.
body.sub: Not mandatory — Cerulean gives you one free at 30 species — but having it now means it is ten levels up by Misty.

body.t: Catch a wild Pikachu (5%) and the 1% Butterfree if you see it.
body.sub: The wild Pikachu is a different Pokémon from your partner. It is the Saffron trade stock for an Alolan Raichu.

body.t: Take the Antidote, both Potions and the Razz Berries scattered through the trees.
Beat the Bug Catchers on the way through.
body.sub: Trainer battles are your only non-catch experience in this game, so none of them are optional if you want to keep pace.

body.t: Take the Potions from Trace and the X Defense behind the Pokémon Center.
Mind the lady’s Slowpoke west of the museum for a Big Pearl.
body.sub: Thirty seconds, and Big Pearls are the cleanest early money in the game.

body.t: Look at the Old Amber in the museum’s employee area, then leave it.
body.sub: It is behind a small tree on the north-east hill. You need Chop Down, which is four stages away — stage 07 is when you come back.

body.t: Show the guide your Oddish or Bulbasaur, then beat Brock.
body.sub: He will not let you in without a Grass or Water Pokémon on your first visit. Geodude 11, Onix 12.

body.t: Take the Great Balls from Blue outside the gym.
body.sub: Blue is the retired Champion here, not your rival. He turns up repeatedly and eventually takes over the Viridian Gym.

body.t: Head east towards Mt. Moon.

stages.title: Mt. Moon — two Moon Stones, and a fossil choice that is no longer permanent
body: Routes 3 and 4 are the sharpest version split in the early game. Let’s Go, Pikachu! gets Sandshrew (20%) and Mankey (20%). Eevee players get Ekans in the Sandshrew slot and nothing at all in the Mankey slot. Both of yours are worth party space; take them now, because Mankey does not appear again and Sandshrew’s only other home is a Celadon trade counter.

body.where: Routes 3 and 4 — 20%, Let’s Go, Pikachu! only
body.why: Take one and build it. Ground is immune to Electric, which makes it a hard counter to the entire Vermilion Gym three stages from now, and it is 2× into Brock’s rematch, Blaine and half of Koga. Read the move note below before you let it evolve.

body.where: Routes 3 and 4 — 20%, Let’s Go, Pikachu! only
body.why: Version exclusive and the only early Fighting type. Karate Chop at 13, Low Kick at 21. Primeape’s 105 Attack carries the mid-game trainer gauntlets until the Fighting Dojo hands you something better.

body.where: Routes 3 and 4 — rare spawn
body.why: The second of the three free-starter rare spawns. If it appears, take it — you are given one on Route 24 anyway, but a second Charmander is a spare Charizard and the Master Trainer for the line is a level-75 fight later.

body.where: Mt. Moon — 4% on 1F and B1F, 9% on B2F
body.why: Clefairy is pure Fairy in this game, not Normal. That means it is immune to Dragon and resists Fighting and Dark, which is a genuinely different Pokémon from the one you remember. Feed it a Moon Stone for Clefable.

body.where: Mt. Moon — 1%
body.why: A 1% cave spawn and the only wild Onix before Victory Road. Chain Geodude if you want to force it; otherwise take it if you see it, because hunting it later is worse.

body.where: Mt. Moon — 15%
body.why: Parasect learns Spore, a sleep move that cannot miss. Nothing else in Kanto has one, and it is the safest way to hold a legendary still later.

body.where: Mt. Moon — 40%
body.why: Golbat at 22 and no further — Crobat needs a friendship evolution that does not exist here. Log it and box it.

body.where: Mt. Moon — 34–40%
body.why: Catch several. Graveler needs a trade to become Golem, but a spare Geodude is what the Vermilion hiker wants for an Alolan Geodude, which is Rock/Electric and exists nowhere else.

body: Take the Sandshrew, and then refuse to let it evolve. Sandshrew learns Dig at 20 and Earthquake at 36. Sandslash learns Earthquake at 52. Evolution in Let’s Go is automatic on level-up unless you hold B through the animation, so hold it: sixteen levels of the best physical Ground move in the game is worth far more than an earlier stat bump. Let it become Sandslash the moment Earthquake is in.

Both Moon Stones are on Mt. Moon B2F, in craters in the closed-off rooms east of the Rocket Grunts. Take both. One is for Clefable; the other is for Nidoking or Nidoqueen if you kept a Nidoran from Route 22. There are more Moon Stones later, but not for a very long time.
At the bottom of Mt. Moon a Super Nerd offers you the Dome Fossil or the Helix Fossil, and takes the other away. In Red, Blue, FireRed and LeafGreen that was a permanent, save-file-ending decision.

It is not permanent here. After you enter the Hall of Fame, the glowing crystal spots in Cerulean Cave respawn fossils on a timer — the plateau beside Mewtwo’s island is guaranteed to hold one, with roughly a 40% chance each of Dome and Helix and 20% of Old Amber. Whichever fossil you refuse today, you can dig up later. Take whichever you like and stop agonising.

Take the Dome Fossil. Kabutops has 115 Attack behind Rock and Water moves that are physical in this generation, so its stats and its STAB point the same way; Omastar has 115 Special Attack and a Rock STAB that is mostly physical. Kabutops is the better Pokémon on the day you revive it — and you can go back for Omanyte in the post-game anyway.

body.where: Mt. Moon B2F — craters in the closed-off rooms
body.why: Clefable, and Nidoqueen or Nidoking. Take both; they do not come back.

body.where: Mt. Moon B2F — plateau in a closed room
Mt. Moon B2F — plateau in the closed room between the stones
Mt. Moon B1F — west of the second ladder
Mt. Moon B2F — from the Super Nerd
body.why: Kabutops at the Cinnabar Lab. The Helix Fossil you refuse can be dug out of Cerulean Cave after the League.

body.where: Route 4 — reward for beating Coach Trainer Oberon
body.why: Coach Trainers are the ones with the exclamation mark; each hands over a TM or a stack of Candy once. Never walk past one.

body.where: Route 4 — hidden in a bush east of the central plateau
Route 4 — between the three rocks west of the Pokémon Center

body: Refuse the Magikarp salesman’s ₽500 on Route 4. Magikarp is a common water spawn on half a dozen routes from Route 4 onwards, and ₽500 is a stack of Great Balls you actually need. Gyarados is worth having — just not for money.

body.t: Catch a Sandshrew and a Mankey — 20% each, and both are Let’s Go, Pikachu! exclusives.
body.sub: Sandshrew is your answer to the Vermilion Gym. Mankey is the only Fighting type available for the next five stages.

body.t: Chain Rattata or Spearow while you walk, and watch for the Charmander rare spawn.
body.sub: A Catch Combo of 31 or more takes rare-spawn odds to 50%. Chaining the common thing is how you force the rare one.

body.t: Clear the trainer line and take the Potion and Poké Balls between the ledges.
Heal, and turn down the Magikarp salesman.
body.sub: ₽500 for a Pokémon that swims freely on Route 4 and half the sea routes.

body.t: Work the cave for Clefairy (4%) and the 1% Onix.
body.sub: Clefairy is pure Fairy here — immune to Dragon, resists Dark and Fighting. It is a real Pokémon in this game, not a Normal-type curio.

body.t: Catch two or three spare Geodude.
body.sub: One becomes an Alolan Geodude at the Vermilion trade counter, and Alolan Geodude is Rock/Electric — a typing that exists nowhere else in Kanto.

body.t: Take both Moon Stones from the craters in the closed-off rooms.
body.sub: East of the Rocket Grunts. One for Clefable, one for a Nidoran line if you kept one.

body.t: Take the Rare Candy and the Nugget from the neighbouring closed rooms.
Take the Big Mushroom west of the second ladder.
body.sub: Big Mushrooms sell for a lot and there is nothing else to spend the detour on.

body.t: Beat the Super Nerd and take the Dome Fossil.
body.sub: Kabutops. And unlike the old games this is reversible — Cerulean Cave respawns fossils after the League.

body.t: Beat Coach Trainer Oberon for TM57 Pay Day.
body.sub: Coach Trainers carry a one-time reward each. Treat every exclamation-mark trainer as a mandatory stop for the rest of the game.

body.t: Take the PP Up hidden east of the central plateau, and the Escape Rope by the three rocks.
Carry on east into town with 30 species logged.
body.sub: Thirty is the number that buys a free Bulbasaur in Cerulean and the IV Judge on Route 11. If you are short, the Mt. Moon caves are the fastest place to make it up.

stages.title: Cascade Badge — Misty, and the first of your three free starters
body: Three things in this town matter more than the badge, and two of them are easy to walk past.

Go to the Pokémon Center and find the Tamer by the counter. He is a Move Tutor and he teaches your partner Zippy Zap — Electric, physical, 50 power, and it is always a critical hit at +2 priority. A guaranteed crit means it ignores any Defense boost the target has set up, and moving first every turn means your Pikachu closes out fights that a slower attacker would lose. It is the single best thing that happens to your team in the first half of the game. Take it before you fight Misty.

body.where: Free from the girl in the house next to the Pokémon Center — needs 30 species caught
body.why: Take it and put it in the party. Venusaur is one of only four Pokémon you can Mega Evolve on the main story, its Grass STAB answers Misty, Giovanni and Brock’s rematch, and it arrives at level 12 already.

body.where: Trade a Rattata to the girl on the Pokémon Center sofa — repeatable
body.why: Dark barely exists in Kanto. This is your first Dark type and it is repeatable, so trade as many as you like. Alolan Raticate is not a party member, but the typing is a Pokédex entry you cannot get any other way.

body.where: Routes 24 and 25 — 20%
body.why: Golduck is a fine Water body if you would rather not wait for Lapras. More usefully, Psyduck is on Misty’s own team, so the species is worth logging early.

body.where: From the Team Rocket Grunt in the robbed house, after you beat him
body.why: 80 power physical Ground. Put this on your Sandshrew immediately if it has not reached level 20 yet — it is the move that wins the next gym.

body.where: From the Bike Maniac in the south-west house, after examining every bicycle
body.why: Heart Scales buy moves back from the Move Reminder at the Indigo Plateau. Five of them free is worth two minutes of listening to a man describe bikes.

body.where: Behind the Gym Badge man’s house
South-west corner of town, south of the hedge wall
From Misty
body.why: 80 power special Water with a 30% burn. A burn halves the target’s physical damage, which makes Scald the best status-inflicting attack in the game.

body: Misty checks your party at the door. The guide will not let you in unless you can show a Pokémon of level 15 or higher. If your team is under-levelled, the Nugget Bridge trainers one screen north are the fix — but you cannot reach the far side of Route 24 without passing them anyway, so do the gym first and come back if you are turned away.

body.name: Misty

team.note: Confusion, Water Gun. Both are weak; Confusion exists to punish the Poison types you might bring.
Scald, Swift, Psywave. Scald can burn; Swift never misses. 100 Special Attack behind 115 Speed — this one is real.

plan: Lead Bulbasaur. Vine Whip is 2× on both, and Grass resists Water back. Take note that Vine Whip and Razor Leaf are physical in this generation and Bulbasaur’s Attack is 49 — they still win here, but this is your first sign that the Bulbasaur line wants special moves from TMs later.
Zippy Zap the Starmie. Electric is 2×, the crit is guaranteed, and at +2 priority you hit before a 115-Speed Starmie ever moves. This is exactly the fight the Cerulean tutor exists for.
Starmie is Water/Psychic, so do not lead with a Poison type — Psywave and Confusion both come through at full or better.
Bring a Burn Heal. Scald burning your physical attacker turns a two-turn win into a five-turn one.
Neither of Misty’s Pokémon has a Grass-effective move at all. If you are carrying Bulbasaur this fight is essentially a formality.
body.reward: TM29 Scald, the Cascade Badge, and obedience up to level 30.

body: Trace fights you again on the way to Nugget Bridge, immediately after the gym. Same three Pokémon as before — Pidgey, Oddish and his Eevee — a few levels up. Heal before you leave the gym; the game does not give you a break between the two.

body.t: Find the Tamer by the counter and learn Zippy Zap.
body.sub: Electric, physical, 50 power, always a critical hit, +2 priority. Do this before the gym, not after.

body.t: Trade a spare Rattata to the girl on the sofa for an Alolan Rattata.
body.sub: Dark/Normal, repeatable, and the only early Dark type in the game.

body.t: Collect the free Bulbasaur from the house next to the Pokémon Center.
body.sub: Requires 30 species caught. It arrives at level 12 — put it straight into the party and start closing the level gap.

body.t: Listen to the Bike Maniac describe every bicycle for five Heart Scales.
body.sub: South-west house. Heart Scales are the currency for the Move Reminder at the Indigo Plateau — you will want them before the Elite Four.

body.t: Take the Rare Candy behind the Gym Badge man’s house and the Burn Heal in the south-west.
Beat the Team Rocket Grunt in the robbed house in the north-east for TM10 Dig.
body.sub: 80 power physical Ground. This is the Vermilion Gym answer if your Sandshrew has not hit level 20.

body.t: Show the guide a level-15 Pokémon, then beat Misty.
body.sub: Psyduck 18, Starmie 19. Bulbasaur leads, Zippy Zap finishes the Starmie.

body.t: Beat Trace as you head for the bridge.
body.sub: Pidgeotto, Oddish and his Eevee. Heal first — the game gives you no gap.

body.t: Cross Nugget Bridge.

stages.title: Nugget Bridge, a free Charmander, and Bill
body: Route 24 is Nugget Bridge — five trainers who must be beaten in sequence, a Nugget at the end, and a man who reveals himself as a Rocket Grunt and fights you for the insult. Route 25 runs east from it to Bill’s Sea Cottage.

body.where: Free from the boy on the north-west hill of Route 24 — needs 50 species caught
body.why: The most important free Pokémon in the game. Charizard gets two Mega Stones, 109 Special Attack, and is one of the three Pokémon you can ride through the sky after the League. Arrives at level 14. Put it in the party now.

body.where: Routes 24 and 25 — rare spawn
body.why: The third free-starter rare spawn. Vermilion gives you one anyway at 60 species, so this is a spare — but a spare Blastoise is a second Master Trainer fight and a Pokédex insurance policy.

body.where: Routes 24 and 25 — 30%
body.why: Venomoth at 31, and Venomoth is on Koga’s gym team. Log it now while it is 30% of the grass.

body.where: Routes 5, 6, 7 and 8 — 5%
body.why: Abra teleports away the instant you approach it in the overworld. Sneak up from behind, and feed it a Razz Berry the moment the throw screen opens. Alakazam needs a trade, but Kadabra is a perfectly good Psychic body on its own.

body: Chansey is a rare spawn on almost every route in Kanto, from Route 5 onwards. It is the single richest experience payout in the game, and it also carries Candy. If a Chansey appears, stop what you are doing, feed it a Razz Berry and throw Ultra Balls — it flees readily and it is worth more than the twenty Pidgey you would otherwise catch on that route.

body.where: Route 24 — from the man at the north end of Nugget Bridge
Route 25 — north of the path
body.why: Paralysis cuts Speed and costs the target a quarter of its turns. It is how you hold a legendary still later without risking a knockout.

body.where: Route 25 — reward for beating Coach Trainer Amala
body.why: Fixed damage equal to the user’s level, and it ignores type resistance entirely. Genuinely useful on anything that struggles to hurt a wall.

body.where: Route 25 — by the fence south-west of Lass Haley
Route 24 — east side of the north-west plateau
Route 5 — from Trace at the Underground Path entrance

body: The bush north-east of Nugget Bridge is one of the game’s walking-Pokémon berry spots. Let a Pokémon out of its ball, walk it over the bush repeatedly, and it will turn up Razz, Silver Razz and occasionally Golden Razz Berries. Golden Razz Berries are what you throw at Articuno, Zapdos, Moltres and Mewtwo — start stockpiling now, because you cannot buy them.

body.t: Beat all five Nugget Bridge trainers in sequence, then take the Nugget.
body.sub: The man handing it over is a Rocket Grunt. He fights you immediately.

body.t: Collect the free Charmander from the boy on the north-west hill.
body.sub: Requires 50 species caught. If you are short, chain the Venonat and Psyduck here — the count is the only thing standing between you and a Charizard.

body.t: Work the bush north-east of the bridge with a walking Pokémon for Razz Berries.
body.sub: This spot can yield Silver and Golden Razz Berries. Golden Razz is what catches legendaries; you cannot buy it anywhere.

body.t: Watch for the Squirtle rare spawn while you clear the route.
Take the Razz Berry ×3 on the east side of the north-west plateau.
Take TM16 Thunder Wave north of the path.
body.sub: Paralysis is your legendary-catching tool. Put it on something that outspeeds.

body.t: Beat Coach Trainer Amala for TM15 Seismic Toss.
Take the Ether by the fence and the hidden Nanab Berries south of the ponds.
Rescue Bill from his own teleporter and take the S.S. Ticket.
body.sub: Talk to the Pokémon in the machine, then to Bill. The ticket is the only way onto the S.S. Anne, which is the only source of Chop Down.

body.t: Go back through town and south onto Route 5.
body.sub: You cannot go east yet — that tree needs Chop Down, which is on the ship.

body.t: Catch an Abra (5%) and a Growlithe (20%, Let’s Go, Pikachu! only).
body.sub: Abra teleports away if it sees you coming — approach from behind and berry it immediately.

body.t: Take the Revives from Trace at the Underground Path, and the Great Balls on the third ledge.
Continue south to Vermilion City.

stages.place: Route 6 · Vermilion City · S.S. Anne · Vermilion Gym
stages.title: Thunder Badge — the S.S. Anne, Chop Down, and a cat you can ride

body.where: Free from Officer Jenny at the north entrance — needs 60 species caught
body.why: The third free starter, at level 16. You are not going to field all three, but Blastoise is a Mega, a Master Trainer fight and a Pokédex line — take it and box it.

body.where: Free from the Black Belt west of the Poké Mart, after catching five Growlithe — Let’s Go, Pikachu! only
body.why: Do this errand. It is the best quality-of-life reward in the game. This Persian can be ridden, which moves you faster than running for the rest of the run. Eevee players get a rideable Arcanine for catching five Meowth instead; you get the cat.

body.where: Trade a Geodude to the hiker on the Pokémon Center sofa — repeatable
body.why: Rock/Electric exists nowhere else in the game. Repeatable, so trade every spare Geodude you took out of Mt. Moon.

body.where: Routes 5, 6, 7 and 8 — 20%, Let’s Go, Pikachu! only
body.why: Catch five of these. One is the Persian errand, one is your Fire body for the rest of the game, and the rest are Candy. Read the evolution warning below before you touch a Fire Stone.

body: Do not evolve Growlithe. Growlithe learns Flamethrower at 17, Heat Wave at 24, Crunch at 28, Outrage at 31, Play Rough at 35 and Flare Blitz at 38. Arcanine learns nothing after evolving — its level-up list is four moves it already has. Hold B through every level-up until Flare Blitz is in at 38, then feed it the Fire Stone. An early Arcanine is a permanently worse Arcanine.

Show the S.S. Ticket at the pier and the ship opens up: two decks of trainers, a cabin full of items, Trace waiting outside the captain’s quarters, and — after you rub the captain’s back — the reason you are here.

Chop Down is the first Secret Technique. Your partner learns it from the captain, it takes no move slot, it is used from the field menu rather than in battle, and it replaces Cut. That is the pattern for all five: they belong to the Pikachu, not to your party, and they never cost you an attack. Once you have it, five things you walked past open up — the tree by the Vermilion Gym, the Old Amber in Pewter, the east side of Cerulean, TM11 in Viridian, and the east half of Route 2.

The ship sails the moment you leave, and it never comes back. Sweep both decks completely before you step off: Full Heal, Elixir, Super Potion, Paralyze Heal, Super Repel, Revive and a Nugget, plus every trainer on board. There is no second visit.

body.where: S.S. Anne 2F — fourth room, past the two Gentlemen
S.S. Anne 1F — the kitchen
S.S. Anne 2F — second cabin from the left
S.S. Anne B1F — the middle cabin
S.S. Anne — the captain’s quarters, after helping him
body.why: Secret Technique. Costs no move slot. Cuts the small trees blocking the Vermilion Gym, Pewter Museum, east Cerulean and east Route 2.

body.where: From Lt. Surge
body.why: 90 power special Electric with a paralysis chance. Your partner already learns it at 21 — put this one on something else, or skip it and keep Zippy Zap.

body.where: Vermilion City — behind the person on the bench east of the Fan Club
body.why: Needs Sea Skim. Come back in stage 12.

body.name: Lt. Surge

team.note: Thunderbolt, Swift, Light Screen. The Light Screen halves your special damage for five turns — hit it physically.
Thunderbolt, Sonic Boom. Electric/Steel means Ground is 4× on it.
Thunderbolt, Quick Attack, Double Kick. Double Kick is 2× on Rock and Steel, so an Alolan Geodude is not the answer here.

plan: Lead your Sandshrew and use Dig. Ground is immune to Electric, so all three of Surge’s Pokémon are throwing Thunderbolts at a Pokémon that cannot be hit by them, and Dig is 2× back into everything he owns and 4× into Magnemite.
If Sandshrew has not reached level 20 for Dig by level-up, TM10 Dig from the Cerulean Rocket Grunt does the same job.
Do not bring your partner. Electric on Electric is resisted both ways, Raichu outstats a Pikachu, and Zippy Zap into a Light Screen is a waste of a guaranteed crit.
Voltorb’s Light Screen only touches special damage. Dig, Karate Chop and Headbutt all go straight through it.

The gym door is behind a small tree — you must have Chop Down from the S.S. Anne before you can reach it. Inside, the barrier needs two switches hidden in the bins: find the first, and the second is always in an adjacent bin. Get it wrong and both reset.
body.reward: TM36 Thunderbolt, Lt. Surge’s Autograph, the Thunder Badge, and obedience up to level 40.

body: The Pokémon Fan Club chairman gives you a free Pikachu outfit for listening to him, and a Raichu set later once you and your partner are best friends. Cosmetic — but partner friendship is not: it drives Pika Papow’s power, and a maxed-out friendship also gives every Pokémon in the party up to a 10% boost to all stats. Play with your partner, feed it Candy and let it walk beside you.

body.t: Catch five Growlithe across Routes 5 and 6 before you reach town.
body.sub: 20% each on both routes, Let’s Go, Pikachu! only. Five is the exact number the Vermilion errand wants.

body.t: Take the free Squirtle from Officer Jenny at the north entrance.
body.sub: Requires 60 species caught. Level 16, and the last of the three free starters.

body.t: Tell the Black Belt west of the Poké Mart you prefer Growlithe, catch five, and come back for a rideable Persian.
body.sub: Riding it is permanently faster than running. This is a five-minute errand with an all-game payoff.

body.t: Trade a spare Geodude on the Pokémon Center sofa for an Alolan Geodude.
body.sub: Rock/Electric — a typing that appears nowhere else in the Kanto dex. Repeatable.

body.t: Listen to the Pokémon Fan Club chairman for the Pikachu clothing set.
Show the S.S. Ticket to the sailor and board the ship.
Sweep both decks completely before you go near the captain.
body.sub: Full Heal on B1F, Paralyze Heal and Super Repel on 1F, Revive and a Nugget on 2F, plus every trainer. The ship sails when you leave and never returns.

body.t: Beat Trace outside the captain’s quarters.
body.sub: Pidgeotto 20, Oddish 20, Eevee 21. His Oddish has Sleep Powder now — lead something fast.

body.t: Help the captain and learn Chop Down.
body.sub: Your first Secret Technique. It takes no move slot and it is used from the field menu, not in battle.

body.t: Chop the tree in the south-west to open the gym.
Solve the two-bin switch puzzle and beat Lt. Surge.
body.sub: Find the first switch; the second is always in an adjacent bin. Voltorb 25, Magnemite 25, Raichu 26 — lead Sandshrew and Dig.

body.t: Speak to Misty outside afterwards.
body.sub: She points you at the Diglett’s Cave entrance on Route 11, which is where you are going next.

body.t: Head east out of Vermilion.

stages.place: Route 11 · Diglett's Cave · Route 2 (east) · Pewter City
stages.title: Diglett’s Cave, Light Up, and the loop back for everything Chop Down opened
body: Route 11 runs east out of Vermilion into the south end of Diglett’s Cave, which tunnels all the way under Kanto and comes out on the east side of Route 2 — the half of that route you could not reach before Chop Down.

body.where: Route 11 — 5%
body.why: Psychic/Fairy in this game, not pure Psychic. That gives it an immunity to Dragon and a resistance to Fighting and Dark on top of the Psychic half. 120 base Special Defense makes it a genuine special wall, and it is on Sabrina’s team so you will meet it again.

body.where: Diglett’s Cave — 85%
body.why: Catch a stack. Dugtrio learns Earthquake at level 29 by itself, which is far earlier than anything else you own gets it, and a spare Diglett is what the Lavender trade wants for an Alolan Diglett — Ground/Steel, and unavailable anywhere else.

body.where: Diglett’s Cave — 5%
body.why: A pre-evolved catch is free levels. Note that a Dugtrio caught here is past level 29 and may already have Earthquake.

body.where: Route 11 — 25%
body.why: Hypno at 26. A perfectly serviceable Psychic body if you would rather not chase the 5% Mr. Mime, and it learns Dream Eater by level-up.

body: Take the Light Up reward as soon as you surface on Route 2. One of Oak’s aides is in the house by the cave mouth and hands your partner Light Up for having caught ten different species — a bar you cleared before Viridian Forest. It lights Rock Tunnel, which is the next stage and is otherwise navigated in the dark.
Chop Down opened four things behind you. None of them is far, and three of them are permanently missable if you forget.

body.where: Pewter Museum — employee area, behind the small tree on the north-east hill
body.why: The one that people never go back for. It becomes Aerodactyl at the Cinnabar Lab — Rock/Flying, 130 Speed, 105 Attack, and the second of the three post-game sky rides.

body.where: Viridian City — from the sleeping man in the south-west, behind a tree
body.why: A guaranteed burn. It halves the target’s physical damage and chips it every turn — the cleanest way to neuter Bruno’s Machamp and Blue’s Tauros later.

body.where: Route 2 east — south of the gate, past the first ledges
body.why: Vileplume from a Gloom, or Victreebel on the Eevee version. Take it even if you are not running a Grass type; stones are a Pokédex requirement.

body.where: Route 2 east — north of Diglett’s Cave
Route 2 east — south of the second pair of ledges
Route 2 — the house by Diglett’s Cave, for 10 species caught
body.why: Secret Technique. Lights dark caves; costs no move slot.

body.where: Route 11 gate — from Oak’s aide, for 30 species caught
body.why: Unlocks the IV readout on every Pokémon’s summary screen. This is how you find out whether the Snorlax you are about to spend an hour raising is worth it.

body: Turn the Judge function on and use it. Let’s Go has no Effort Values — those are replaced by Awakening Values that you feed with Candy — but it still has ordinary IVs, and a Pokémon caught at the end of a long Catch Combo comes with guaranteed perfect IVs in some stats. From here on, before you commit to raising something, check the Judge screen. A 31-Speed Dugtrio and a 0-Speed Dugtrio are different Pokémon.

body.t: Speak to Oak’s aide in the east gate for the Judge function.
body.sub: Needs 30 species. It adds an IV readout to every summary screen — use it before you invest in anything.

body.t: Catch a Mr. Mime (5%) and a couple of Drowzee while you are here.
body.sub: Mr. Mime is Psychic/Fairy in this game, with 120 Special Defense. It is a real wall, not a novelty.

body.t: Catch five or six Diglett on the way through.
body.sub: 85% of the cave. One becomes an Alolan Diglett at the Lavender trade counter; the rest are Candy and experience.

body.t: Enter the house by the cave mouth and take Light Up.
body.sub: Ten species caught. It lights Rock Tunnel, which you walk into next stage.

body.t: Chop the trees and take the Leaf Stone, the Great Balls and the Super Potion.
body.sub: South of the gate, past the ledges. The Leaf Stone is a Pokédex requirement even if you never field a Grass type.

body.t: Chop the tree on the museum’s north-east hill and take the Old Amber.
body.sub: This is the single most-forgotten item in Kanto. It becomes Aerodactyl at the Cinnabar Lab, and Aerodactyl is one of your three sky mounts after the League.

body.t: Chop the tree in the south-west and take TM11 Will-O-Wisp from the sleeping man.
body.sub: A guaranteed burn halves physical damage for the rest of the fight. Save it for Bruno.

body.t: Chop the tree on the east side of town.
body.sub: Trace offers to walk you here from Route 2 if you accept his invitation — take it, it saves the whole trip back through Mt. Moon.

body.t: Head east towards Rock Tunnel.

stages.place: Route 9 · Route 10 · Rock Tunnel · Lavender Town
stages.title: Rock Tunnel, a 1% Kangaskhan, and a tower you cannot climb yet
body: Rock Tunnel is pitch black without Light Up and merely inconvenient with it. Use it. Underneath the darkness it is a straightforward two-floor loop with a heavy trainer count and one genuinely valuable spawn.

body.where: Rock Tunnel — 1%
body.why: Stop and hunt this. Rock Tunnel is the only place in the game a Kangaskhan appears in the wild, it is fully evolved at level 18–23, and its Master Trainer is one of the 145 fights you will want later. Chain Geodude or Zubat to push the rare rate up.

body.where: Rock Tunnel — 10%
body.why: Machoke at 28 and no further without a trade — Machamp is a trade evolution and it still is one here. Machoke is a fine Fighting body regardless, and Machamp’s Master Trainer is unavoidable, so catch several and find a trading partner eventually.

body.where: Rock Tunnel — 9%, and Pokémon Tower at 10%
body.why: Marowak at 28. More importantly, a spare Marowak is what the Fuchsia trade wants for an Alolan Marowak — Fire/Ghost, and one of the better Pokémon in the game.

body.where: Rock Tunnel — 10%
body.why: Rhydon at 42. 130 Attack behind a Ground/Rock body; it is on Giovanni’s gym team and it is worth having your own.

body.where: Rock Tunnel — 10%
body.why: Ten times commoner here than in Mt. Moon. If you missed the 1% one, this is where you fix that.

body.where: Rock Tunnel — rare spawn
body.why: A third chance at a Charmander, in a cave where you will be walking past hundreds of spawns anyway.

body: Pokémon Tower stops you on the third floor and nothing you do will change that. The ghost blocking the stairs cannot be identified without the Silph Scope, and the Silph Scope is in the Rocket Hideout under the Celadon Game Corner. Do the trainers on 1F and 2F, take the items you can reach, and come back in two stages. Do not spend an hour trying to get past it.

body.where: Trade a Diglett in the Lavender Pokémon Center — repeatable
body.why: Ground/Steel, and it exists nowhere else. Alolan Dugtrio keeps Earthquake and adds a Steel typing that resists Fairy, Dragon, Rock and Ice. Repeatable, so trade every spare Diglett.

body.where: Pokémon Tower 3F–6F — 70–75%
body.why: You cannot reach these floors yet, but note the rate: Gastly is three-quarters of the tower. Haunter at 25, and Gengar is a trade evolution — the same wall as Machamp.

body.where: Route 9 — hidden in the south-east corner, east of Hiker Alan
body.why: Pinap Berries double the Candy a catch gives you. Save them for anything you intend to raise.

body.where: Route 9 — middle of the route
Rock Tunnel 1F — south-west corner
Rock Tunnel B1F — north-east of Black Belt Dudley
Rock Tunnel B1F — north-east corner
Rock Tunnel B1F — north-east section
Pokémon Tower 1F — from the old lady
Pokémon Tower 2F — reward for beating Coach Trainer Holly
body.why: Species Candy raises any Awakening Value on that species. Five of them on your partner is a real stat gain.

body: Between Rock Tunnel’s north entrance and Lavender you will be ambushed by four Rocket Grunts and rescued by Lorelei of the Elite Four, who takes three of them herself. You only fight one. Nothing is missable here — just do not walk into it on a red team.

body.t: Clear the trainers and take the hidden Pinap Berry ×5 in the south-east, and the Poké Ball ×5 in the middle of the route.
body.sub: Pinap doubles Candy from a catch. Worth hoarding for Chansey and for anything you plan to raise.

body.t: Use Light Up before you go in.
body.sub: Not mandatory, but the cave is genuinely unnavigable without it.

body.t: Hunt the 1% Kangaskhan.
body.sub: This is the only wild Kangaskhan in the game. Build a Catch Combo on Geodude or Zubat first — 31 or more takes the rare-spawn rate to 50%.

body.t: Catch Machop, Cubone, Rhyhorn and Onix on the way through.
body.sub: Cubone is the trade stock for an Alolan Marowak in Fuchsia. Machop is the Machamp line, which needs a trade partner eventually.

body.t: Take the Pearl on 1F, and the Dire Hit, Great Balls and Full Heal on B1F.
Beat the Rocket Grunt after Lorelei scatters the other three.
Trade a Diglett in the Pokémon Center for an Alolan Diglett.
body.sub: Ground/Steel. Repeatable, and the typing appears nowhere else.

body.t: Clear 1F and 2F, then turn around.
body.sub: Take the Formal Set from the old lady and beat Coach Trainer Holly for five Pikachu Candy. The ghost on 3F needs the Silph Scope, which is in Celadon.

body.t: Beat Trace on 2F.
body.sub: Pidgeotto 27, Gloom 27, Jolteon 28 — his Eevee has evolved. Ground moves answer the Jolteon; nothing he owns is dangerous.

body.t: Head west out of Lavender towards Celadon.

stages.place: Route 7 · Route 8 · Celadon City · Rocket Hideout
stages.title: Rainbow Badge — Erika, the Rocket Hideout, and Sky Dash
body: Routes 7 and 8, on the way in

body.where: Routes 7 and 8 — 1%, Let’s Go, Pikachu! only
body.why: A fully evolved Arcanine in the wild, and this is the best rare hunt in the mid-game. Chain Growlithe here — they are 19% of the grass — and at a combo of 31 the rare rate hits 50%. A caught Arcanine skips the entire Fire-Stone-timing problem.

body.where: Routes 7 and 8 — 1%
body.why: Saves you evolving an Abra. Alakazam is still a trade evolution, so Kadabra is where a solo player stops — 120 Speed and 105 Special Attack is plenty.

body.where: Route 7 — rare spawn
body.why: Note this now. Silph Co. gives you one free at level 34 in two stages, but Porygon is a rare spawn here and nowhere else in Kanto — a spare is a second Master Trainer entry and insurance.

body.where: Trade a Sandshrew in the Celadon Pokémon Center — repeatable, Let’s Go, Pikachu! only
body.why: Ice/Steel is a typing no other Pokémon in the game has. Alolan Sandslash has 120 Defense and 100 Attack. Eevee players trade for an Alolan Vulpix here instead.

body: Visit the Celadon Pokémon Center Move Tutor before the gym and take Floaty Fall. Flying, physical, 90 power, 95 accuracy, 30% flinch — and it is 2× into Erika’s entire team. Your partner’s Attack is 80, so a 90-power physical move is the hardest thing it can throw. This is the second of its three exclusive moves.

The Celadon Gym only admits Trainers with a “cute” Pokémon. The Lass at the door wants to see one before she moves. Your partner Pikachu qualifies, so this gate costs you nothing — but it will stop you dead if you have somehow left it behind.

Five floors and a roof. The roof vending machines sell Fresh Water, Soda Pop and Lemonade — Lemonade is the cheapest healing per point in the game and there is no reason to buy Hyper Potions while it exists. The TM counter on 4F is where you fill the gaps in your movepool for money rather than for exploration.

body.where: Route 8 — inside the fenced tall grass, behind a small tree
body.why: This is your Arcanine stone. Do not use it until Growlithe has Flare Blitz at 38.

body.where: Route 8 — often found by a walking Pokémon at the bush on the west side
body.why: Golden Pinap is both a catch-rate boost and a Candy multiplier. This bush is one of the reliable sources.

body.where: Route 7 — reward for beating Coach Trainer Alpesh
body.why: 70 power, and it doubles to 140 while the user is burned, poisoned or paralysed. It is the answer to Koga’s Toxic stalling two stages from now.

body.where: Celadon City — near the north-west corner
Celadon Department Store 3F — from the man behind the counter
body.why: Boosts an ally’s move by half. There are no double battles in the story, so this is an index entry rather than something you will ever select.

body.where: Celadon City — near the north-east corner
From Erika
body.why: 75 power in Let’s Go, not the 40 it is in every other game — the buff makes it functionally Giga Drain, and it still heals for half the damage dealt. Put it on Venusaur immediately; see the note below on why its level-up Grass moves are the wrong ones.

body.where: Celadon City — from the man north of the pond
body.why: Needs Sea Skim. Come back in stage 12.

body.where: Rocket Hideout B3F — south of the stairs from B2F
body.why: 80 power special Dark. This is your Sabrina answer — put it on Arcanine, whose 100 Special Attack turns it into a real threat.

body.where: Rocket Hideout B2F — centre of the northern spinner maze
Rocket Hideout B4F — thrown onto the overhead grating
body.why: Send your partner up the vent from the chair to walk the pipes and fetch it. Without it the lift does not run and Giovanni is unreachable.

body.where: Rocket Hideout B4F — from Giovanni, after you beat him
body.why: The item Pokémon Tower has been waiting for.

body.where: Celadon City — from the Rocker outside the Game Corner, after the Silph Scope
body.why: Secret Technique. Flies you to anywhere you have already visited. This is the moment the game stops being a walking simulator.

body: Venusaur is a TM platform, not a level-up Pokémon. Its level-up Grass moves — Vine Whip 45, Razor Leaf 55, Power Whip 120 — are all physical, and Venusaur has 82 Attack against 100 Special Attack. The moves that match its stats are Petal Dance (which it learns free on evolving), Mega Drain from Erika, TM52 Sludge Bomb and TM45 Solar Beam. Evolve it the moment it hits 32 — Venusaur gains Petal Dance on evolution, so unlike Growlithe there is no reason to hold it back.

body.name: Erika

team.note: Mega Drain, Sleep Powder, Bind. Sleep Powder is the only real threat — it is 75% accurate and sleep lasts.
Mega Drain, Poison Jab. Poison Jab is physical and hurts if you lead something frail.
Mega Drain, Moonblast. Moonblast is Fairy — 95 power special — and it is the move people are not expecting from a Grass gym.

plan: Lead Charmeleon or Charizard. Fire is 2× on all three, and Ember/Heat Wave off a 109 Special Attack ends this gym in three turns.
Floaty Fall on your partner is 2× on everything she owns, at 90 power off an 80 Attack, with a 30% flinch. Take it from the Celadon tutor before you walk in.
Two of her three are Grass/Poison, which means Psychic is also 2× — a Kadabra or Mr. Mime does the same job if you have no Fire.
Do not bring a Water or Ground type. Both are resisted by Grass and neither of them threatens back.
Bring Awakenings. Tangela’s Sleep Powder is the only way this fight goes wrong, and Vileplume’s Moonblast punishes a Fighting or Dark answer.
body.reward: TM53 Mega Drain, the Rainbow Badge, and obedience up to level 50.

body: Behind the poster in the Game Corner, four floors down, two spinner-tile mazes and a Grunt who throws the Lift Key onto the overhead grating out of spite. Send your partner up through the vent — move the blue chair under it first — and walk it along the pipes to retrieve the key. Jessie and James are guarding the last room and hear it moving, but mistake it for Meowth’s stomach.

body.name: Giovanni

team.note: Slash, Feint, Fake Out. Fake Out flinches you on turn one, so expect to lose your opening move.
Drill Run, Take Down, Megahorn, Rock Throw. Ground/Rock is 4× weak to both Water and Grass.

plan: Venusaur ends the Rhyhorn in one move — Grass is 4× into Ground/Rock. Mega Drain heals you back up while it does it.
Persian has no super-effective move against anything reasonable and 65 base HP. Any Fighting move removes it; your partner’s Double Kick still works.
Do not open with a slow setup turn. Fake Out is guaranteed to flinch on the first turn Persian is out, so your lead simply loses that turn.
This is the same Giovanni you fight twice more — once in Silph Co. and once as the eighth Gym Leader. His team grows each time but the shape does not change.
body.reward: The Silph Scope, which unlocks the top of Pokémon Tower — and, once you have it, the Rocker outside the Game Corner teaches your partner Sky Dash.

body.t: Chop into the fenced grass and take the Fire Stone.
body.sub: Hold it. Growlithe wants to reach level 38 and Flare Blitz before you use it.

body.t: Chain Growlithe (19%) and hunt the 1% Arcanine.
body.sub: A wild Arcanine is fully evolved and skips the stone-timing problem entirely. At a combo of 31+ the rare rate is 50%.

body.t: Work the west-side bush with a walking Pokémon for a Golden Pinap Berry.
body.sub: Golden Pinap is both a catch-rate boost and a Candy multiplier, and it cannot be bought.

body.t: Beat Coach Trainer Alpesh for TM12 Facade.
body.sub: 70 power that doubles to 140 while you are burned, poisoned or paralysed. Remember it when you reach Koga.

body.t: Watch for the Porygon rare spawn.
body.sub: Silph Co. gives you one free in two stages, but this is the only place a second one exists.

body.t: Learn Floaty Fall from the Move Tutor.
body.sub: Flying, physical, 90 power, 30% flinch — and 2× into every Pokémon Erika owns.

body.t: Trade a Sandshrew for an Alolan Sandshrew.
body.sub: Ice/Steel. No other Pokémon in the game has that typing. Repeatable.

body.t: Take the Tea from Brock outside the Condominiums.
body.sub: He also hands over Pewter Crunchies. The Tea is what gets you past the Saffron City guards two stages from now — do not skip this conversation.

body.t: Shop the Department Store: Lemonade on the roof, TMs on 4F, evolution stones on 4F.
body.sub: Lemonade is the cheapest healing in the game by a wide margin. Stop buying Hyper Potions.

body.t: Take the Rare Candy in the north-west and the Nugget in the north-east.
Show the Lass your partner Pikachu, then beat Erika.
body.sub: Tangela 33, Weepinbell 33, Vileplume 34. Vileplume’s Moonblast is Fairy — do not lead a Dark or Fighting type.

body.t: Beat the Grunt by the poster in the Game Corner and press the switch underneath.
Clear B1F to B3F, taking TM20 Dark Pulse and TM05 Rest.
body.sub: Dark Pulse is your Sabrina answer — put it on Arcanine, which has 100 Special Attack.

body.t: Move the blue chair under the vent and send your partner along the pipes for the Lift Key.
body.sub: The Grunt throws it onto the overhead grating. There is no other way up.

body.t: Beat Jessie and James, then Giovanni, and take the Silph Scope.
body.sub: Persian 35 and Rhyhorn 35. Venusaur removes the Rhyhorn in one move — Grass is 4× on Ground/Rock.

body.t: Speak to the Rocker outside the Game Corner and learn Sky Dash.
body.sub: He only appears once you hold the Silph Scope. This is Fly, it costs no move slot, and it changes how the rest of the game feels.

body.t: Sky Dash back to Lavender.
body.sub: You now have the Silph Scope. The tower is open.

stages.title: Pokémon Tower, Marowak, and the Poké Flute
body: With the Silph Scope in your bag the tower opens all the way to the top. Floors 3 to 6 are three-quarters Gastly, which makes this the densest Ghost hunting in the game and the only sensible place to build that part of the Pokédex.

body.where: Pokémon Tower 3F–6F — 70–75%
body.why: Catch a handful. Haunter at 25 comes free from levelling, but Gengar is a trade evolution and it still is one in this game — so keep spares against the day you find someone to trade with. Gengar’s Master Trainer is one of the 145.

body.where: Pokémon Tower 3F–6F — 5–10%
body.why: Skips the levelling. Same trade wall for Gengar, but a wild Haunter at level 27–32 is immediately usable.

body.where: Pokémon Tower 3F–6F — 10%
body.why: If you did not get one in Rock Tunnel, get one here. Marowak at 28, and a spare Marowak becomes an Alolan Marowak at the Fuchsia trade counter — Fire/Ghost, 110 Defense, and a genuinely good Pokémon.

body.where: Pokémon Tower 3F–6F — rare spawn
body.why: The single biggest experience payout in the game, and it appears as a rare spawn on almost every route and in most caves. Feed it a Razz Berry and throw Ultra Balls — it flees easily.

body: Ghost is not what it was in Generation I. Ghost moves hit Psychic for 2× and are resisted by Dark; Normal and Fighting cannot touch a Ghost type at all. Just as importantly, Steel no longer resists Ghost or Dark — that resistance was removed in Generation VI. If you learned Kanto on the old games, this is one of the corrections that will actually cost you a fight.

The Marowak on 6F is not a battle. The Silph Scope reveals it, its spirit is calmed, and Trace takes the Cubone home. There is nothing to catch and nothing to lose — do not burn a Master Ball’s worth of anxiety on it.

body.where: Pokémon Tower 2F — south-west corner
Pokémon Tower 2F — reward for beating Coach Trainer Holly
body.why: Species Candy raises any one Awakening Value on that species. Feed all five to your partner.

body.where: Pokémon Tower 4F — south-west of the centre
body.why: Teleport was reworked for this game. It is no longer an escape button: it now switches the user out at −6 priority, so it always goes last, and it fails if the user is your only healthy Pokémon. Take it for the index rather than for a move slot.

body.where: Pokémon Tower 3F — hidden in the north-east corner
Pokémon Tower 5F — near the north-east wall

stages.place: Saffron City · Silph Co. · Fighting Dojo · Saffron Gym
stages.title: Marsh Badge — Silph Co., the Master Ball, and Sabrina
body: The Saffron Gym requires a Pokémon of level 45 or higher to enter. This is the hardest gate in the game and it will stop you if you have been rushing. Silph Co. is eleven floors of trainers — do all of them, and you will clear the bar on the way out. If you are still short, the Fighting Dojo next door and the Route 7 and 8 trainers are the top-up.

Warp panels connect the floors in a deliberately confusing order. The route below is the short one. Trace joins you for a Multi Battle against Archer on 5F, which is where the Card Key comes from, and Giovanni is waiting on 11F.

body.where: Silph Co. — free from the office worker on 7F, at level 34
body.why: Take it. Porygon has exactly two homes in this game — this gift and a rare spawn on Route 7 — and Porygon2 requires a trade, so the base form is what you keep. It is also a Master Trainer fight later.

body.where: Fighting Dojo — choose one, at level 30
body.why: Take Hitmonlee over Hitmonchan. 120 Attack against 105, and it arrives with Brick Break already learnt at 20, Jump Kick at 30 and High Jump Kick at 45. Hitmonchan’s elemental punches look wider but run off a 35 Special Attack — its own stats fight its moveset.

body.where: Trade a Raichu in the Saffron Pokémon Center — repeatable
body.why: Electric/Psychic exists nowhere else. You need a Raichu to trade — evolve the wild Pikachu you caught in Viridian Forest with a Thunder Stone. Your partner cannot evolve, so it is safe.

body: Put TM20 Dark Pulse on Arcanine before you fight Sabrina. Dark is 2× into Psychic, Arcanine has 100 Special Attack, and Dark Pulse is 80 power special with a flinch chance. That single TM, from the Rocket Hideout floor you cleared last stage, is the difference between a comfortable gym and a slog — because Kanto simply does not give you a good Dark type.

body.where: Silph Co. 2F — from the woman in the north-west room
Silph Co. 5F — from Trace, after the Multi Battle against Archer
body.why: Opens every locked door in the building. Without it most of the tower is closed.

body.where: Silph Co. 5F — south-west room
body.why: 80 power special Steel. Steel is 2× into Fairy, Rock and Ice — and note that it no longer resists Ghost or Dark on defence.

body.where: Silph Co. 7F — eastern room
body.why: 85 power special Dragon. Hold it for Lance; Dragon is 2× into Dragon and nothing else you meet before then.

body.where: Silph Co. 10F — south-west room
body.why: 90 power special Fire. Charizard has 109 Special Attack and does not learn it until level 54 — this TM saves you twenty levels.

body.where: Silph Co. 11F — from the president, after Giovanni
body.why: One only, and it never misses. Save it for Mewtwo. Every other legendary in the game can be worn down and caught with Golden Razz Berries and Ultra Balls; Mewtwo is level 70 with the worst catch rate in Kanto.

body.where: Silph Co. 7F and 10F — one on each

Nidoqueen’s Crunch is 2× into Psychic, so keep Kadabra and Mr. Mime out of this one.
He is 39s against your 40s. This is a checkpoint, not a wall — the real Giovanni fight is the eighth gym.

body.name: Sabrina

team.note: Psychic, Reflect, Light Screen, Double Slap. It is Psychic/Fairy here — Dark is neutral, not super effective — and it sets both screens.
Psychic, Yawn, Surf, Calm Mind. Yawn puts you to sleep a turn later; Calm Mind makes it worse the longer it lives.
Psychic, Lovely Kiss, Ice Punch. Lovely Kiss is a 75%-accurate sleep and it is the fight-loser.
Psychic, Night Shade. 135 Special Attack and 120 Speed — but only two moves and paper defences.

plan: Lead Arcanine with Dark Pulse. Dark is 2× into three of the four, off a 100 Special Attack, and Arcanine’s 95 Speed outruns everything except Alakazam.

Kill Mr. Mime first. It is not a threat itself, but Reflect and Light Screen make the other three take twice as long, and Mr. Mime being part Fairy means your Dark move is only neutral into it. Hit it with your hardest physical attack instead — Floaty Fall from your partner is neutral but enormous, and Mr. Mime has 65 Defense.
TM13 Brick Break destroys Reflect and Light Screen on hit. If you have it, one Brick Break undoes the whole gym’s strategy.
Bring Awakenings, and more than one. Jynx’s Lovely Kiss and Slowbro’s Yawn both put you to sleep, and a sleeping lead against four Psychics is how this gym is lost.

Alakazam has 55 HP and 45 Defense. Anything physical that connects removes it — your partner’s Zippy Zap moves first at +2 priority and always crits, which is exactly the answer to a 120-Speed glass cannon.

stages.title: Soul Badge — the first Snorlax, Pokémon Road, and Sea Skim
body: There is no Bicycle in this game and Cycling Road is now Pokémon Road. You walk it, or you ride the Persian you earned in Vermilion. Nothing is gated behind a bike, and there is no bike to buy — the Cerulean bike shop exists only to give you five Heart Scales.

Snorlax is an interactive Pokémon: you must battle it and knock it out before you can throw a ball. That is true of both Snorlax, of the disguised Electrode in the Power Plant, and of every legendary in the game. The rules of an interactive encounter are: a five-minute timer that does not pause for the HOME button or sleep mode, boosted stats — Snorlax gets an Attack or Defense boost, legendaries get a lift on everything — and at least three perfect IVs guaranteed on whatever you catch. Save before you play the flute.

Take the Route 16 Snorlax into your party and drop Primeape for it. 160 HP, 110 Attack and 110 Special Defense on a body that has no weakness except Fighting. It arrives around level 34 with Headbutt and Rest, learns Body Slam at 52, Crunch at 58 and Superpower at 65, and it is the Pokémon that survives the Elite Four’s worst turns. Feed it a Golden Razz Berry before you throw — a five-minute fight you have to redo is a five-minute fight wasted.

body.where: Route 16 — wake with the Poké Flute, then battle it
body.why: The best non-legendary body in the game. Interactive encounter: defeat it inside five minutes, then throw. Guaranteed three perfect IVs. There is a second one on Route 12 — catch both, because a spare Snorlax is a level-75 Master Trainer fight later.

body.where: Route 17 — 5%
body.why: The only wild Eevee in Let’s Go, Pikachu! — and it is a plain Eevee, not a partner Eevee. You need it for Vaporeon, Jolteon and Flareon, which are three separate Pokédex entries and three separate Master Trainers. Catch four.

body.where: Route 17 — 20%
body.why: Rapidash at 40. Genuinely fast — 105 base Speed — and it is on Blaine’s and Trace’s teams.
Dodrio at 31, and Dodrio is also wild here at 5–10%. Two dex entries for the price of a walk.

body.where: Trade a Marowak in the Fuchsia Pokémon Center — repeatable
body.why: Fire/Ghost, 110 Defense, and it exists nowhere else. Raise a Cubone from Rock Tunnel or the Tower to 28 and trade it. Immune to Normal and Fighting, and it burns things.

body: The Fuchsia Gym will not let you in until you have caught 50 different species. Not 50 Pokémon — 50 species. If you have been throwing at everything as instructed you passed this two stages ago; if you have been running past spawns, you are about to find out. The Safari Zone next door and the four routes you just walked are the fastest way to make it up.
The Safari Zone and GO Park

The Safari Zone is not a catching minigame any more. The old preserve is split in two: the Playful Park, a walk-through zoo, and the GO Park complex, twenty pens holding fifty Pokémon each for transfers out of Pokémon GO. There are no Safari Balls, no step limit and no fleeing rules — and the man by the Lapras exhibit in the Playful Park teaches your partner Sea Skim, which is this game’s Surf.

Take Splishy Splash from the Fuchsia Move Tutor. Water, special, 90 power, 30% paralysis — and it is the last of your partner’s three exclusive moves. It matters more than it looks: Pikachu’s only weakness is Ground, and Splishy Splash is 2× back into Ground and Rock. With Zippy Zap, Floaty Fall and Splishy Splash your partner covers Water, Flying and Electric off two different attack stats, and nothing in Kanto walls all three.

body.where: Pokémon Road — reward for beating Coach Trainer Grantley
body.why: 80 power physical Ground with a raised critical-hit rate. The best Ground move you can hand a physical attacker before Giovanni.

body.where: Route 16 — from the reclusive girl in the north house, behind a tree
body.why: This is the battle move, not the Secret Technique. Sky Dash already handles travel. Fly is 90 power physical Flying with a turn spent in the air — situational, and worth taking for the Pokédex completionist reasons alone.

Pokémon Road — grass south of the water
Pokémon Road — small yellow bush at the north-east corner of the southern field
Playful Park — the man by the Lapras exhibit, west of the Poké Mart

body.why: Badly poisons — damage that escalates every turn. It is how you break a wall you cannot out-damage, and it is what Koga just did to you.

body.name: Koga

team.note: Toxic, Protect, Sludge Bomb, Explosion. Explosion is 250 power and it will take your lead with it.
Toxic, Protect, Sludge Bomb, Moonblast. The Fairy move is there to punish a Fighting or Dark answer.
Toxic, Protect, Fly, Leech Life. Poison/Flying is 2× weak to Electric, Ice, Psychic and Rock.
Sludge Bomb, Protect, Psychic, Bug Buzz. Bug/Poison is 4× weak to Psychic and 2× to Flying, Fire and Rock.

plan: Ground is the type that beats this gym. Poison takes 2× from Ground, and Sandslash’s Earthquake or a Dugtrio removes three of the four. Golbat is the exception — it is part Flying, so Ground does nothing to it.
Bring your partner for the Golbat. Electric is 2× into Poison/Flying, and Zippy Zap moving first with a guaranteed crit ends it before Fly gets off the ground.
Venomoth is 4× weak to Psychic. One Psychic from Kadabra, Mr. Mime or anything holding TM40 removes it outright.

The gym’s whole plan is Toxic, then Protect — badly poison you, then stall while the damage escalates. Answer it two ways: carry Antidotes, and if a Pokémon does get poisoned, TM12 Facade doubles to 140 power while the status is on it. Coach Trainer Alpesh on Route 7 gave you that TM for exactly this fight.
Do not stand in front of the Weezing at low HP. Explosion is 250 base power and Koga will use it.

body.sub: Fire/Ghost — immune to Normal and Fighting, 110 Defense. Repeatable.

body: Fairy is the type that most changes how Kanto plays. Clefairy and Clefable are pure Fairy; Jigglypuff, Wigglytuff and Mr. Mime are part Fairy. Fairy is 2× into Dragon, Dark and Fighting and it is immune to Dragon entirely, which is the reason a Clefable answers Lance’s Dragonite in a way nothing in the old games could. It is walled by Steel, Fire and Poison. TM32 Dazzling Gleam is your only way to put it on a Pokémon that does not have it naturally — take it here.

stages.title: Articuno, and the Lapras that finishes your team
body: Lapras is a rare spawn on the water of Routes 19 and 20, and it is the sixth member of your team. Water/Ice with 130 HP: it is the answer to Lance’s entire Dragon roster, to Giovanni’s Ground types, and to Blaine. It learns Ice Beam at 39 and Surf at 45 by itself, so it needs almost nothing from you. Chain Tentacool on Route 19 — 30% of the surf table — to force the rare spawn, and drop Sandslash for it. If your buddy is a Lapras you also ride it during Sea Skim instead of the partner.

body.where: Sea Routes 19 and 20 — rare spawn on the water
body.why: Chain Tentacool and hunt this properly. There is no gift Lapras in this game and no other source. Ice Beam at 39, Surf at 45, 130 base HP, and it answers Lance.

body.where: Route 19 — 30% on the water
body.why: Starmie with a Water Stone: 115 Speed, 100 Special Attack, and Water/Psychic. There is a wild Starmie at 1% here too if you want to skip the stone.

body.where: Seafoam Islands — 15%
body.why: Dewgong at 34, and it is wild here at 10%. Water/Ice bulk, and a fixture on Lorelei’s team.

body.where: Seafoam Islands — 14%
body.why: 115 Special Attack behind Ice/Psychic. Seafoam is the only place it lives, and Lorelei brings one to the League.

body.where: Seafoam Islands — 15%
body.why: Slowbro at 37, and wild Slowbro is 10% here. Slowbro is on Sabrina’s, Lorelei’s and Trace’s teams — worth having your own.

body.why: Cloyster with a Water Stone: 180 base Defense. Wild Cloyster is 1% on the same water.

body.why: Interactive encounter. Level 50, all stats boosted, five-minute timer, at least three perfect IVs, and it will never flee — so you can throw at it all day once it is down.

body: Do not bring a Rock move to Articuno. Ice/Flying is 4× weak to Rock, and a Rock Slide from a level-50 physical attacker will simply kill it. You want it at a sliver of health, not dead. Bring Electric (2×, and your partner’s Zippy Zap is a guaranteed crit you can control) or Fire (2×, Arcanine), whittle it down, and stop.

The catching kit for every legendary in this game is the same: a stack of Ultra Balls, a stack of Golden Razz Berries from the daily bush spots, and patience. Feed a Golden Razz, throw with a good spin for the multiplier, and remember that Articuno, Zapdos, Moltres and Mewtwo never run away — unlike every ordinary wild Pokémon, you cannot lose them by missing. The only way to lose an interactive Pokémon is to let the five-minute battle timer expire, and then it just resets.

body.where: Seafoam Islands B2F — south area
body.why: 90 power special Ice. Lapras learns it at 39 anyway; put this copy on Starmie or Blastoise.
