body.name: Articuno

team.note: All stats boosted, as every legendary in this game is. Ice/Flying: 4× Rock, 2× Fire, Electric and Steel; resists Grass, Bug and Ground; immune to Ground.

plan: Save before you play. The battle is on a five-minute timer that does not pause for the HOME button or sleep mode. If it expires the fight simply ends and you start again — but a save is still the cheapest insurance.
No Rock moves. Rock is 4× and will overkill it. Use Electric or Fire and stop when it is nearly out.
Your partner’s Zippy Zap is ideal: Electric is 2×, the damage is predictable, and +2 priority means you always get the last word before it acts.
Once it faints the throwing screen opens. Feed a Golden Razz Berry, aim for an Excellent throw, and keep going — Articuno never flees. A missed ball costs you a ball, nothing else.
It is Ice/Flying, so it is immune to Ground. Leave Sandslash and Dugtrio on the bench for this one.
body.reward: A level-50 Articuno with at least three perfect IVs. Catching all three birds is one of the two conditions for them respawning in the sky after the League.

body.t: Chain Tentacool on the water and hunt the Lapras rare spawn.
body.sub: 30% of the surf table, and Lapras has no other source in the game. A chain of 31+ takes the rare rate to 50%.

body.t: Catch a Staryu (30%) and watch for the 1% wild Starmie.
Take the Heart Scale by the southern Seafoam entrance and the Ultra Balls on Roger’s island.
Speak to the Poké Mart clerk outside the cave for a free full heal of your team.
Strong Push the first two boulders down the holes in the floor.
body.sub: Both must fall through. This is what eventually blocks the currents on B3F.

body.t: Beat Coach Trainer Yas for five Rare Candies.
Take TM55 Ice Beam in the south and the Ice Stone on the south-east plateau.
body.sub: The Ice Stone is what evolves your traded Alolan Sandshrew.

body.t: Push the remaining boulders down through B1F and B2F until they land in the water on B3F.
body.sub: Two sets of two. When all four are in the sea the currents stop and Sea Skim works down here.

body.t: Solve the second boulder cluster and drop through to B4F.
body.sub: Push the right-hand boulder to the north wall, the left one two south and one west, the one south of the ladder all the way west, then drop the last two through the gaps.

body.t: Save, then battle and catch Articuno.
body.sub: Level 50, all stats boosted, five-minute timer. Electric or Fire only — Rock is 4× and will kill it.

body.t: Take the Big Pearls on the water’s edge and climb back out through B3F.
body.sub: Collect the Ultra Balls, Super Lure and the Ice Stone on the way up if you have not.

body.t: Sea Skim west along Route 20.

stages.place: Cinnabar Island · Pokémon Mansion · Cinnabar Gym
stages.title: Volcano Badge — three fossils, a burnt mansion, and a quiz show
body: You are not limited to one fossil Pokémon here. Hand the scientist in the Testing Room whichever fossils you are carrying and he revives each one on the spot — Helix into Omanyte, Dome into Kabuto, Old Amber into Aerodactyl, all at level 44. The only limit is which fossils you own, and Cerulean Cave respawns the ones you refused at Mt. Moon after the League. Revive everything you have.

body.where: Cinnabar Lab — revive the Dome Fossil, level 44
body.why: Kabutops at 40, so it evolves almost immediately. 115 Attack behind physical Rock and Water STAB — the stats and the moves point the same way.

body.where: Cinnabar Lab — revive the Old Amber, level 44
body.why: 130 Speed and 105 Attack. This is the Pokémon you went back to Pewter for in stage 07 — and after the League it becomes one of your three sky mounts.

body.where: Cinnabar Lab — revive the Helix Fossil, level 44
body.why: Only if you took Helix at Mt. Moon. Omastar has 115 Special Attack and 125 Defense; it is the slower, tankier half of the fossil pair.

body.where: Trade a Grimer in the Cinnabar Pokémon Center — repeatable, Let’s Go, Pikachu! only
body.why: Poison/Dark, and Grimer is a Let’s Go, Pikachu! exclusive. Alolan Muk has 105 HP and 105 Attack and is immune to Psychic-boosting nonsense. Eevee players trade for an Alolan Meowth here instead.

body.where: Pokémon Mansion — 15%
body.why: The only place Magmar lives. 100 Special Attack; Magmortar does not exist in this game, so this is the whole line.

body.where: Pokémon Mansion — 10%
body.why: Do not skip this. The Pokémon Mansion is one of only two homes for Ditto. There is no breeding in this game so Ditto has no mechanical use at all — it is purely a Pokédex entry and a Master Trainer, and it is easy to leave the island without one.

body.where: Pokémon Mansion — 15%, Let’s Go, Pikachu! only
body.why: Version exclusive, and the trade stock for Alolan Grimer downstairs. Catch several.

body: Four floors of statues that flip hidden switches, opening one door and closing another. The route below is the shortest path that also collects everything. The Secret Key is in the last room of the basement and the gym does not open without it.

body.where: Cinnabar Lab Research Room — from the scientist at the desk
body.why: Forces the target to use damaging moves only. It shuts down Koga’s Protect stalling and Sabrina’s screens in one turn.

body.where: Pokémon Mansion 2F — reward for beating Coach Trainer Rita
body.why: 75 power physical Rock with a flinch chance. Note it and keep it away from the legendary birds — Rock is 4× on all three.

body.where: Pokémon Mansion 3F — north-east room
body.why: Dark, and it uses the target’s Attack rather than yours. Excellent on a bulky Pokémon against Bruno’s Machamp.

body.where: Pokémon Mansion B1F — the southern room
body.why: 90 power special Poison. This is the move Venusaur has been waiting for — same-type, special, and it matches its 100 Special Attack.

body.where: Seafoam Islands B2F — already collected last stage
body.why: Listed again as a reminder: if your Lapras is not carrying it, Madame Memorial at the Indigo Plateau will teach it for a Heart Scale.

body.where: Pokémon Mansion 1F south — past the potted plants
body.why: A second Fire Stone. If Growlithe has reached 38 and taken Flare Blitz, use one now.

body.where: Pokémon Mansion B1F — the final room to the south
body.why: Opens the Cinnabar Gym. Nothing else does.

body.where: Pokémon Mansion 3F south-west, B1F north-central, and 2F
From Blaine
body.why: 110 power special Fire at 85% accuracy. Charizard’s 109 Special Attack turns it into the hardest single hit you can throw before Hyper Beam.

body.name: Blaine

team.note: Flamethrower, Low Kick, Confuse Ray. Confuse Ray is the annoyance — it costs you turns at random.
Flare Blitz, Quick Attack, Fury Attack. Flare Blitz recoils, so it damages itself for you.
Fire Blast, Quick Attack. 81 Special Attack and 109 Speed; the Fire Blast is 110 power and will hurt.
Flare Blitz, Outrage, Crunch. Outrage is 120 power Dragon and it is the move that catches people out in a Fire gym.

plan: Lead Lapras. Water is 2× into all four, Water/Ice resists Fire back, and 130 base HP means even the Fire Blast does not threaten it. Surf or Ice Beam ends most of them in one.
Ground works on the ones that stand still — Sandslash’s Earthquake is 2× on every one of them and none of Blaine’s Pokémon is part Flying.

Arcanine’s Outrage is Dragon, so a Dragon or a Fairy answer matters more than a Water one against that slot. If you took TM32 Dazzling Gleam on Route 12, a Clefable eats Outrage for nothing — Fairy is immune to Dragon.
Carry Burn Heals. Every Pokémon here can burn you, and a burn halves your physical damage, which turns a three-turn win into a seven-turn one.

Blaine will not fight you until you have won his five-question quiz — or lost enough of it to have beaten five of his students. Either route gets you five Blaine dolls; getting the questions wrong just means more battles.
body.reward: TM46 Fire Blast, the Volcano Badge, and obedience up to level 80.

body.t: Trade a Grimer in the Pokémon Center for an Alolan Grimer.
body.sub: Poison/Dark. Grimer is a Let’s Go, Pikachu! exclusive and it lives in the mansion up the road — catch a few first if you have none.

body.t: Take TM02 Taunt from the scientist in the Research Room.
Revive every fossil you are carrying in the Testing Room.
body.sub: Dome into Kabuto, Helix into Omanyte, Old Amber into Aerodactyl — all at level 44, and there is no limit on how many you hand over.

body.t: Catch Ditto (10%), Magmar (15%) and several Grimer (15%).
body.sub: The mansion is one of only two places Ditto exists, and Ditto has no use in this game beyond the Pokédex — which is exactly why people forget it.

body.t: Work the four floors, flipping the statue switches as you go.
body.sub: Each statue opens one door and closes another. Read the four journal entries on the way — they are the Mewtwo backstory.

body.t: Beat Coach Trainer Rita on 2F for TM22 Rock Slide.
Take TM21 Foul Play on 3F and TM52 Sludge Bomb in the basement.
body.sub: Sludge Bomb is 90 power special Poison — the STAB move Venusaur’s stat spread has been waiting for.

body.t: Take the three Rare Candies scattered through the mansion.
body.sub: 3F south-west, B1F north-central, and one on 2F. The mansion is the densest Rare Candy in the game.

body.t: Take the second Fire Stone in the south of 1F.
body.sub: If Growlithe has hit 38 and learnt Flare Blitz, this is the moment to use it.

body.t: Take the Secret Key from the last room in the basement.
Answer Blaine’s five questions, then beat him.
body.sub: Magmar 47, Rapidash 47, Ninetales 47, Arcanine 48. Lead Lapras; carry Burn Heals; watch for Arcanine’s Outrage.

body.t: Sea Skim north towards Pallet Town.

stages.place: Route 21 · Pallet Town · Route 10 · Power Plant
stages.title: Zapdos, and the Key Stone that unlocks Mega Evolution
body: Sea Skim north from Cinnabar along Route 21 to Pallet, then Sky Dash to the Route 10 Pokémon Center and Sea Skim south down the river past the Rock Tunnel entrance. The Power Plant is a short way along the bank.

Half the items in the Power Plant are Electrode. The disguised ones are white on top and red underneath — the exact reverse of a real Poké Ball. Walk into one and it is an interactive battle with a five-minute timer, like a Snorlax. That is not a punishment: an Electrode you defeat and catch comes with three guaranteed perfect IVs, so take every one you find.

body.where: Power Plant — the final room, north-west
body.why: Interactive encounter, level 50, all stats boosted. Electric/Flying is 4× weak to Rock and 2× to Ice — same trap as Articuno. Use Ice, not Rock. It never flees.

body.where: Power Plant — uncommon
body.why: The only place it lives. Electivire does not exist here, so Electabuzz is the whole line — and it is on Lt. Surge’s rematch team.

body.where: Power Plant — disguised as items
body.why: Interactive encounters with three guaranteed perfect IVs. 150 base Speed. Catch every one.

body.where: Power Plant — uncommon
body.why: 120 Special Attack. Electric/Steel resists an enormous list, and Magnezone does not exist here.

body.where: Power Plant — uncommon
body.why: A fully evolved spawn. Saves you levelling the Grimer you caught on Cinnabar.

body: Let’s Go has Mega Evolution and it is easy to walk past. After the Power Plant, Trace drags you back to Oak’s lab, where Blue hands you the Key Stone plus the Venusaurite, Charizardite X, Charizardite Y and Blastoisinite. There are no held items in this game, so a Mega Stone sits in your Bag and applies to that species automatically — you simply get a Mega button in battle. One Mega per battle, it lasts until the fight ends, and the only other stones are the Mewtwonite X and Y that Green gives you in Cerulean Cave after the League, plus a merchant at the Indigo Plateau who sells the rest.

Charizardite Y is the one to use. Mega Charizard Y takes Charizard’s 109 Special Attack to 159 and keeps Fire/Flying; Mega Charizard X trades the Flying half for Dragon and pushes Attack instead, which fights against everything Charizard’s level-up moves do. If you have followed this guide your Charizard is holding Flamethrower and Fire Blast, both special — so Y, and it is not close. Venusaurite is the fallback if you want a wall rather than a cannon.

body.where: Power Plant — north-east room
body.why: Raichu, Jolteon. You need a Raichu to trade for an Alolan Raichu in Saffron, so this is the one that pays for itself.

body.where: Power Plant — south-east area
body.why: 110 power special Electric at 70% accuracy. Big, and unreliable — Thunderbolt is the better everyday move.

body.where: Power Plant — hidden in the long horizontal room in the centre
Power Plant — north-east of the entrance
Power Plant — reward for beating Coach Trainer Mable
Oak's Lab — from Blue
body.why: Enables Mega Evolution. One Mega per battle, and it wears off when the battle ends.

body.n: Venusaurite · Charizardite X · Charizardite Y · Blastoisinite
body.where: Oak's Lab — from Blue, all four at once
body.why: No held items in this game: the stone lives in your Bag and unlocks the Mega button for that species.

body.where: Route 21 — reward for beating Coach Trainer Pam
Route 21 — Fisherman Nolan's island

body.name: Zapdos

team.note: All stats boosted. Electric/Flying: 4× Rock, 2× Ice; resists Fighting, Flying, Steel, Grass and Bug; immune to Ground.

plan: Ice, not Rock. Rock is 4× and will kill it outright. Lapras’ Ice Beam at 90 power off an 85 Special Attack is exactly the controlled damage you want.
It is immune to Ground and resists Fighting, Steel, Grass, Bug and Flying — so Sandslash, Hitmonlee and Venusaur are all wasted slots here.
Electric does nothing special back at you, but Zapdos’ own Electric moves are boosted. Do not send Lapras in at low health.
The five-minute timer applies. If it expires the fight ends and Zapdos is still there — nothing is lost but the time.
Zapdos never flees. Golden Razz, Ultra Balls, and keep throwing.
body.reward: A level-50 Zapdos with at least three perfect IVs — the second of the three birds you need before they start appearing in the sky.

body.t: Sea Skim north from Cinnabar, beating Coach Trainer Pam for TM35 Ice Punch.
body.sub: Also take the Water Stone on Fisherman Nolan's island and the PP Up on the island nearest Cinnabar.

body.t: Sky Dash to the Route 10 Pokémon Center, then Sea Skim south down the river.
body.sub: Past the Rock Tunnel entrance. The Power Plant is a short way along the east bank.

body.t: Take the Thunder Stone in the north-east room.
body.sub: Evolve your spare wild Pikachu with it — a Raichu is what the Saffron trade counter wants for an Alolan Raichu.

body.t: Catch every Electrode disguised as an item.
body.sub: White on top, red underneath — the reverse of a real Poké Ball. Each one is an interactive battle with three guaranteed perfect IVs.

body.t: Take the Max Revive north-east of the entrance, the hidden Voltorb Candy in the long central room, and the Rare Candy ×5 from Coach Trainer Mable.
Catch Electabuzz, Magneton and Muk.
body.sub: The Power Plant is the only home for Electabuzz in the game.

body.t: Take TM38 Thunder in the south-east and beat Coach Trainer Mable for five Rare Candies.
Save, then battle and catch Zapdos in the final room.
body.sub: Level 50, all stats boosted. Ice Beam only — Rock is 4× and will kill it.

body.t: Sky Dash to Viridian and find Trace outside the still-locked gym.
body.sub: He walks you back to Pallet automatically. This is scripted; you cannot skip it.

body.t: Take the Key Stone and all four Mega Stones from Blue at Oak’s lab.
body.sub: Venusaurite, Charizardite X, Charizardite Y, Blastoisinite. Charizardite Y is the one you will actually use.

body.t: Talk to the girl in the flower patch outside.
body.sub: She tells you the Viridian Gym Leader is back. This is the trigger; the gym stays shut until you have heard it.

body.t: Sky Dash back to Viridian.

stages.title: Earth Badge — Giovanni, for the third and last time
body: The Viridian Gym has no entry requirement beyond the seven badges you already hold — the guide says earning those was hard enough. Inside it is green spinner tiles and yellow stoppers, and the path is fixed.

The spinner route, in order: north-east from the entrance until you hit a fence; beat Ace Trainer Samuel to the south-west; take the green tiles west to the yellow stopper on the west wall, which pulls Tamer Cole out of position; spin north for Ace Trainer Kelly; follow the north and east walls to the south-east corner for Ace Trainer Yuji and a Revive; spin west from the entrance to the south-west corner; then take the blue tiles into the centre, beat Tamer Jason and Black Belt Takashi, and step on the yellow stopper. The lights come on and Giovanni is in the office.

body.name: Giovanni

team.note: Slash, Sucker Punch, Earthquake. 120 Speed — it moves first and Sucker Punch is Dark at +1 priority, so it punishes a Psychic answer.
Super Fang, Earthquake, Crunch. Super Fang halves your current HP regardless of type.
Megahorn, Earthquake, Poison Jab, Horn Drill. Horn Drill is a one-hit KO at 30% accuracy — there is no defending against it, only outspeeding it.
Earthquake, Rock Slide, Megahorn. Ground/Rock is 4× weak to both Water and Grass.

plan: Lead Lapras and lead with Surf. Water is 2× into everything he owns and 4× into Rhydon, and Lapras’ 130 HP absorbs an Earthquake without complaint.
Venusaur is the other half of the answer — Grass is 4× on Rhydon and 2× on the rest, and being part Poison it takes Nidoking’s Poison Jab at half. Mega Venusaur if you want the fight to be boring.
Leave your partner on the bench. Electric does nothing to three of the four and is a straight zero into Dugtrio, Nidoqueen and Nidoking. Splishy Splash is the exception — bring it out only for that.
Nidoking’s Horn Drill is a 30%-accurate one-hit knockout. You cannot resist it. Kill Nidoking quickly rather than tanking it, and keep a Revive within reach.
Dugtrio’s Sucker Punch is Dark and has priority, so a Kadabra or Mr. Mime lead loses the turn it needed. Do not open Psychic.
body.reward: TM41 Earthquake, the Earth Badge, and obedience from every Pokémon you own at any level. Giovanni disbands Team Rocket and leaves; Blue takes over the gym.

body: TM41 Earthquake is the single best physical TM in the game and you get exactly one. 100 power, perfect accuracy, and it is 2× into five types. Put it on Snorlax — 110 Attack, no Ground weakness of its own, and it gives Snorlax an answer to the Electric, Rock, Steel, Fire and Poison types that its Normal STAB struggles with. Sandslash and Dugtrio learn Earthquake by level-up anyway, so do not waste the machine on them.

body.t: Follow the spinner route to the centre and step on the yellow stopper.
body.sub: The full sequence is in the note above. Take the Revive by Ace Trainer Yuji in the south-east corner on the way.

body.t: Beat every Ace Trainer on the way in.
body.sub: They are the last easy experience before Victory Road, and you want level 60 before the League.

body.t: Beat Giovanni and take TM41 Earthquake.
body.sub: Dugtrio 49, Nidoqueen 49, Nidoking 49, Rhydon 50. Lapras with Surf; watch for Nidoking's Horn Drill.

body.t: Put Earthquake on Snorlax.
body.sub: 100 power off 110 Attack, and it plugs every hole in a pure Normal movepool. Sandslash and Dugtrio get it free by level-up — do not spend the machine on them.

body.t: Speak to Blue outside as he takes over the gym.
Head west out of Viridian towards the Pokémon League.

stages.title: Victory Road, Moltres, and the last of the boulder puzzles
body: Get every member of your six to at least level 58 before you go through the League doors. The Elite Four run 51 to 55 and Trace finishes at 57 — but the five fights are consecutive with no Pokémon Center between them, so the number that matters is not your level, it is your stock of Full Restores and Revives. Buy twenty of each at the Indigo Plateau mart before you start.

The boulders in Victory Road work differently from the Seafoam ones. There you dropped them down holes; here you push them onto pressure switches that lower stone walls. If you push one into a dead end, leave the cave and come back — the puzzle resets.

body.where: Victory Road 2F — north-west area
body.why: Interactive encounter, level 50, all stats boosted. Fire/Flying is 4× weak to Rock, exactly like the other two birds. Use Water or Electric. It never flees.

body.where: Victory Road 2F — rare spawn
body.why: If you took Hitmonchan at the Dojo, this is where you get the other one. Both are rare spawns in this cave and neither has another source.

body.where: Victory Road 3F — rare spawn
body.why: The other half of the Dojo choice. Chain Machop or Geodude in here to force either one.

body.where: Victory Road — common
body.why: A fully evolved Machoke saves you 28 levels. Machamp still needs a trade, so stock up if you have a partner to trade with.

body.where: Victory Road — common
body.why: 130 Attack, and it is on Giovanni’s rematch team. Rhyperior does not exist here.

body.where: Route 23 south — 1%
body.why: Fully evolved wild Nidoqueen and Nidoking are both 1% here, and both lines are otherwise Moon-Stone evolutions. Chain Nidorina or Nidorino to force them.

body.where: Route 23 south — 1%
body.why: A fully evolved Exeggutor at 1%, or Exeggcute at 14% and a Leaf Stone. You need one either way — an Exeggutor is what the Indigo Plateau trade wants for an Alolan Exeggutor, which is Grass/Dragon.

body.where: Victory Road — south-west of Black Belt Daisuke
body.why: 200 power in this game — not the 120 it is everywhere else. Let’s Go buffed it, and on Venusaur’s 100 Special Attack it is the single biggest hit your team can throw. It still spends a turn charging.

body.where: Victory Road — north-east area
body.why: 120 power physical Fighting that drops your own Attack and Defense afterwards. A finisher, not a staple.

body.where: Victory Road — north-west area
body.why: 110 power special Ice at 70% accuracy. Ice Beam is the reliable one; Blizzard is for when you need the number.

body.where: Victory Road — north area
body.why: Chip damage on switch-in. Of limited use against the Elite Four, who lead into you rather than rotating.

body.where: Victory Road — reward for beating Coach Trainer Ryan
body.why: 120 power physical Dragon that locks you in for 2–3 turns and confuses you afterwards. It is the one Dragon move most of your team can hold.

body.where: Victory Road — reward for beating Coach Trainer Alemana
body.why: Ten species Candy for your partner. Spend it all on one stat — Attack, if you are running Zippy Zap and Floaty Fall.

body.where: Victory Road — north area, behind the boulder puzzle
body.why: You must choose between this and TM56 on the first pass; leave the cave and re-enter to reset the puzzle and take the other.

body.where: Victory Road — southern area, north-east of the paired Ace Trainers
Route 23 — the island north of the fifth checkpoint, via Sea Skim
body.why: Sweep Route 23’s checkpoints with Sea Skim. Golden Razz, Golden Nanab and Golden Pinap are all here in stacks of eight, and this is the best single haul of them in the game.

body.name: Moltres

team.note: All stats boosted. Fire/Flying: 4× Rock, 2× Water and Electric; resists Fighting, Bug, Steel, Fire, Grass and Fairy; immune to Ground.

plan: Rock is 4× — do not use it. Your Snorlax is carrying Rock Slide by now and a level-60 Snorlax will delete a level-50 Moltres with it. Leave Snorlax out of this fight entirely.
Lapras with Surf is the right answer: Water is 2×, the damage is predictable, and Lapras resists Moltres’ Fire back.
Your partner’s Splishy Splash also works — 90 power special Water with a 30% paralysis chance, and paralysis makes the throwing phase easier.
It is immune to Ground and resists Fighting, Bug, Steel, Fire, Grass and Fairy. Half your team does nothing to it.
Third of three. Once Moltres is caught you have the full set, which is one of the two conditions for the birds beginning to appear in the sky after you become Champion.
body.reward: A level-50 Moltres with at least three perfect IVs, and the last of the three stationary birds.

body.t: Beat Trace at the gate.
body.sub: Pidgeot 50, Vileplume 50, Marowak 50, Jolteon 51. His Eevee is a Jolteon in this version — Ground answers it, and Marowak is the one that hits hardest.

body.t: Show all eight badges at the checkpoints, and Sea Skim to every island on the way through.
body.sub: Golden Razz Berry ×8 on the island north of the fifth checkpoint, plus Golden Nanab and Golden Pinap in the same quantities by the seventh. This is the biggest berry haul in the game and you want it before the League.

body.t: Chain Nidorina or Nidorino for the 1% Nidoqueen and Nidoking, and pick up an Exeggutor.
body.sub: An Exeggutor is the trade stock for an Alolan Exeggutor at the Indigo Plateau — Grass/Dragon, and it exists nowhere else.

body.t: Strong Push the first boulder east onto the pressure switch.
body.sub: That lowers the wall on the central ridge. These boulders go onto switches, not down holes.

body.t: Beat Coach Trainer Alemana for ten Pikachu Candy.
body.sub: Spend all ten on one Awakening Value — Attack, if your partner is running Zippy Zap and Floaty Fall.

body.t: Take either the Leaf Stone or TM56 Stealth Rock, then leave and re-enter to reset the puzzle and take the other.
body.sub: The cave is narrow enough that the boulder blocks one to reach the other. Resetting is free.

body.t: Save, then battle and catch Moltres in the north-west.
body.sub: Level 50, all stats boosted. Water or Electric — and keep Snorlax and its Rock Slide well away.

body.t: Take the PP Max south of Moltres, the hidden Pretty Wing on the pillar west of it, and the Golden Nanab Berry ×5 in the southern area north-east of the paired Ace Trainers.
Take TM45 Solar Beam, TM49 Superpower and TM51 Blizzard on the way through.
body.sub: Solar Beam on Venusaur is the biggest Grass hit available to you.

body.t: Beat Coach Trainer Ryan for TM39 Outrage, then take the eastern exit.
Climb the stone staircase to the Pokémon League.

stages.title: The Elite Four, and Trace as Champion
body: Shop before you go up the stairs. Twenty Full Restores, ten Revives, a stack of Max Potions. You cannot leave once you start, healing between rounds comes entirely out of your bag, and running out in Lance’s room means starting the whole gauntlet again.

Visit Madame Memorial by the Pokémon Center first. For one Heart Scale each she will teach any Pokémon any move it can learn by level-up in its current form. This is the Move Reminder, and it is how you undo a bad decision — a Snorlax that missed Body Slam, a Lapras without Ice Beam, an Arcanine that evolved before Flare Blitz. You have at least five Heart Scales from the Cerulean bike shop.

body.where: Trade an Exeggutor to the Super Nerd by the Poké Mart — repeatable
body.why: Grass/Dragon exists nowhere else in any game’s Kanto dex. 125 Special Attack and a straight immunity to the Ground moves that plague Grass types. Bring the Exeggutor you caught or evolved on Route 23.

body.name: Lorelei

team.note: Aqua Jet, Ice Shard, Waterfall. Two priority moves — it gets the first hit whatever you lead.
Lovely Kiss, Psychic, Blizzard. Lovely Kiss is the fight-loser. 75% accurate sleep, and there is no timer on sleep here.
Ice Beam, Spike Cannon, Hydro Pump. 180 base Defense — do not try to punch through it physically.
Surf, Flamethrower, Psychic. The Flamethrower is there for the Grass and Steel types you would bring against the rest.
Blizzard, Dragon Pulse, Hydro Pump. 130 HP and it hits from the special side; expect to spend two or three turns.

plan: Four of her five are part Water, and all but Jynx are part Ice. Electric is the through-line: your partner’s Zippy Zap is 2× on four of the five, always crits, and moves first at +2 priority — which beats Dewgong’s Aqua Jet and Ice Shard.
Grass answers Cloyster and Slowbro where Electric only ties. Venusaur’s Solar Beam or Mega Drain is 2× into both, and Cloyster’s 180 Defense is irrelevant against a special hit.
Fighting handles Jynx — Ice/Psychic takes 2× from Fighting, Bug, Fire, Ghost, Dark and Steel. Hitmonlee’s Brick Break, or a Snorlax carrying Earthquake, ends it before Lovely Kiss lands.
Bring Awakenings and use them immediately. A sleeping lead against five bulky Water types is how this fight goes long enough to run you out of Full Restores in round one.
Do not lead a Ground type. Every one of her Pokémon carries a Water move and Ground takes 2× from all of them.
body.reward: No item — the four rooms run straight into each other. You cannot heal at a Center between them.

body.name: Bruno

team.note: Stealth Rock, Iron Tail, Earthquake. Rock/Ground is 4× weak to Water and Grass.
Fire Punch, Ice Punch, Thunder Punch. Three coverage moves off a 35 Special Attack — they are physical, and they still only chip.
Brick Break, Feint, Rock Slide. Brick Break destroys Reflect and Light Screen if you were relying on either.
Waterfall, Body Slam, Superpower. Water/Fighting is 4× weak to nothing but takes 2× from Grass, Electric, Flying, Psychic and Fairy.
Earthquake, Rock Slide, Superpower. 130 Attack. This is the one that actually threatens you.

plan: Psychic and Flying dismantle four of the five. Charizard’s Air Slash or Heat Wave, Mr. Mime’s Psychic, or your partner’s Floaty Fall — 90 power physical Flying, 2× into Fighting.
Onix and Poliwrath both fold to Venusaur. Grass is 4× on Onix and 2× on Poliwrath, and Venusaur outlives anything they throw.
Machamp is a 130-Attack physical wall-breaker. Burn it — TM11 Will-O-Wisp from Viridian halves its damage for the rest of the fight — or remove it with a Psychic or Flying hit before it sets up.
Fairy is 2× into Fighting. If you brought a Clefable or gave anything TM32 Dazzling Gleam, this is the room it earns its slot in.
Do not send a Dark, Rock, Steel, Ice or Normal type. All five of those take 2× from the Fighting half of his team.
body.reward: Straight through to Agatha.

body.name: Agatha

team.note: Glare, Crunch, Poison Jab. Glare paralyses regardless of type.
Shadow Ball, Will-O-Wisp, Sludge Bomb. The Will-O-Wisp is aimed at your physical attacker.
Air Slash, Crunch, Quick Attack. Air Slash flinches — expect to lose turns.
Sludge Bomb, Shadow Ball, Thunderbolt. The Thunderbolt is for the Water type you would bring.
Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Dazzling Gleam. The Fairy move punishes the Dark answer you were about to bring.

plan: Every one of the five is part Poison, so Ground is 2× on four of them — Golbat is the exception. A Snorlax with Earthquake, or a Sandslash, or a Dugtrio does most of this room on its own.
Psychic is 2× into Poison as well, and both Gengar take it at full — Ghost does not resist Psychic. Mr. Mime, Kadabra or anything carrying TM40 Psychic.
Steel no longer resists Ghost or Dark. If you were planning to wall the Shadow Balls with a Magneton or an Alolan Sandslash, that resistance was removed two generations ago and it will not save you.
The second Gengar carries Dazzling Gleam, which is Fairy and 2× into Dark. Do not bring an Alolan Muk or a Persian expecting to sweep.
Normal and Fighting moves do literally nothing to either Gengar. Snorlax’s Body Slam is a zero — that is what Earthquake is on it for.
body.reward: Straight through to Lance.

body.name: Lance

team.note: Hydro Pump, Dragon Pulse, Hyper Beam. Pure Water despite the room’s theme.
Rock Slide, Earthquake, Hyper Beam. 4× weak to Electric — Rock/Flying is the worst defensive typing in the room.
Waterfall, Iron Tail, Hyper Beam. Also 4× weak to Electric.
Air Slash, Dragon Pulse, Hyper Beam. 4× weak to Rock, 2× to Water and Electric.
Outrage, Fire Punch, Hyper Beam. 4× weak to Ice, and Outrage is 120 power.

plan: Your partner Pikachu is the answer to this entire room. Aerodactyl and Gyarados are both 4× weak to Electric, Charizard is 2×, and Zippy Zap is a guaranteed critical hit at +2 priority. Three of five die before they act.
Lapras handles the Dragonite — Ice Beam is 4× into Dragon/Flying, and Lapras’ 130 HP survives an Outrage if the Ice Beam somehow does not finish it.

Fairy is completely immune to Dragon. A Clefable, or anything carrying TM32 Dazzling Gleam, cannot be touched by Dragonite’s Outrage or Seadra’s and Charizard’s Dragon Pulse at all. If you have one, this is its best room in the game.
Four of the five carry Hyper Beam — 150 power, and then they lose their next turn recharging. Survive it and you get a free turn; plan the switch around that.
Do not bring a Rock type expecting to punish the Flying half. Aerodactyl and Charizard both carry Earthquake or Rock Slide of their own, and Rock is the type this room is best equipped to beat.
body.reward: Straight through to the Champion’s room.

body.name: Trace

team.note: Quick Attack, Air Slash, Heat Wave. The Fire move is there for the Steel and Grass types you brought for the rest.
Solar Beam, Reflect, Sludge Bomb. The Reflect doubles the length of the fight if you are hitting physically.
Fire Punch, Bonemerang, Brick Break. Bonemerang hits twice, which cuts through a Substitute.
Flare Blitz, Quick Attack, Poison Jab. Flare Blitz recoils — it does a third of the work for you.
Psychic, Surf, Light Screen. The second screen. Between this and Vileplume’s Reflect he can halve both your damage types.
Thunder, Quick Attack, Pin Missile. This is the Let’s Go, Pikachu! version of his team — Eevee players face a Raichu here instead. 130 Speed and 110 Special Attack.

plan: Mega Evolve Charizard Y and lead with it. 159 Special Attack, Fire is 2× into Vileplume, and Air Slash or Heat Wave answers four of the six. One Mega per battle — spend it here.
Lapras or your partner for the Marowak: pure Ground takes 2× from Water, Grass and Ice, and Splishy Splash is 2× into it while Zippy Zap is a zero.
Jolteon is the last Pokémon and the fastest thing on the field. Ground is a straight immunity to its Thunder — send Snorlax with Earthquake, or a Sandslash, and it cannot touch you.
TM13 Brick Break breaks Reflect and Light Screen on contact. Between Vileplume and Slowbro he will put both up; one Brick Break removes whichever is standing.
Venusaur is a poor lead here — Pidgeot’s Heat Wave, Rapidash’s Flare Blitz and Slowbro’s Psychic all hit it hard. Bring it out for the Marowak and the Slowbro only.
body.reward: The Hall of Fame, the Champion title, and the ability to ride Charizard, Aerodactyl or Dragonite through the sky — which is also how you meet the legendary birds again.

stages.title: The sky opens — riding, the roaming birds, and 145 Master Trainers
body: You can now ride Charizard, Aerodactyl or Dragonite through the sky. Sky riding does three things at once: it moves you anywhere instantly, it bypasses every Chop Down and Sea Skim obstacle in the game, and it puts you into a layer of the world that has its own encounter table. The Pokémon you meet up there are Flying types you cannot find on the ground — and, once you have caught all three stationary birds, Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres themselves.

body.where: In the sky over most outdoor routes, after catching the Seafoam one
body.why: The birds respawn in the sky, so nothing is missable. Two conditions: enter the Hall of Fame, and catch all three stationary encounters first. They never flee, so a sky sighting is a guaranteed catch if you have the balls for it.

body.where: In the sky, after catching the Power Plant one
body.why: Same rules. A second Zapdos is a second set of at-least-three perfect IVs to compare, and a spare for the Master Trainer’s CP check.

body.where: In the sky, after catching the Victory Road one
body.why: Same rules. Chain the ordinary sky spawns to raise the rare rate before you go hunting.

body.where: In the sky over most routes
body.why: 134 Attack and it is your third sky mount. Dratini and Dragonair are Route 10 water spawns, but a wild Dragonite in the sky skips 55 levels of raising.

body.where: In the sky over most routes
body.why: A wild Charizard means you can field one without spending the Route 24 gift, and it makes a second Charizardite worth buying.

body.where: In the sky
body.why: Fully evolved and common up there. Cheaper than raising the Pidgey you have been ignoring since Route 1.

body: A Youngster outside your house explains them: 153 red-clothed Trainers with a species icon over their head, spread across every route, city and cave in Kanto. Beating one earns you their title.

The Master Trainer rules are strict and unusual. You may bring one Pokémon and it must be the same species as theirs, and it has to sit in the first party slot. No items are allowed — not by you, not by them. Their Pokémon run levels 65 to 80 with maxed Awakening Values, and 69 of the 145 battles are at level 75. You may Mega Evolve and use a Shiny; they may not. Win and you can re-battle the next day; lose and you can ask for an immediate rematch. Nobody loses money either way. The eight Master Trainers for the Legendaries, Mew and Ditto do not battle at all — they want to see a specimen with a high enough CP.

Beat six Master Trainers first, then go to the Indigo Plateau for Red. Six is the exact trigger. Pick six of the level-65 fights — Bulbasaur on Route 4, Charmander in the Celadon Condominiums, Squirtle, Dratini, and the other cheap ones — rather than grinding a level-80 species. Red fights under Master Trainer rules with a full team of six at level 85, so bring your best six and use your Mega.

body.name: Red

team.note: Thunderbolt, Brick Break, Iron Tail, Reflect. The Reflect goes up first and halves your physical damage.
Superpower, Fire Blast, Earthquake, Hyper Beam. 130 Attack and four ways to hurt you.
Heat Wave, Crunch, Will-O-Wisp, Roar. Roar forces your Pokémon out and picks the replacement for you.
Ice Shard, Waterfall, Body Slam, Megahorn. Entirely physical, which is odd for a Lapras and means Reflect-style answers do not help.
Toxic, Protect, Rest, Body Slam. It will Toxic you and stall. This is the slot that runs the clock.
Mega Venusaur. Sludge Bomb, Mega Drain, Leech Seed, Amnesia. Amnesia doubles its Special Defense; Leech Seed drains you while it does.

plan: No items, on either side. Bring six healthy Pokémon and expect to trade knockouts. This is the one battle in the game where a Full Restore is not the answer.
Kill the Snorlax and the Mega Venusaur early. Both of them win by stalling — Toxic and Protect on one, Leech Seed and Amnesia on the other. The longer they live the worse your position gets.
Ground is the through-line: 2× into his Pikachu and Arcanine, and Earthquake is on his own Machamp for a reason. A Sandslash or a Snorlax carrying TM41 does real work.
Psychic and Flying answer the Machamp before Superpower connects. Mega Charizard Y’s Air Slash or a Mr. Mime’s Psychic.
Watch for Roar from the Arcanine — it drags your lead out and replaces it at random, so do not build a position around one Pokémon staying in.
You need six Master Trainer wins before Red appears at all, and you must approach him with a full party of six.
body.reward: The title Battle Master, usable in link battles. He returns for a rematch every time you re-enter the Hall of Fame.

body.sub: All fully evolved, all in the air, and all far cheaper than raising the base forms.

body.sub: Pick the level-65 ones: Bulbasaur on Route 4, Charmander in the Celadon Condominiums, Squirtle, Dratini. Six is the exact number that spawns Red.

stages.title: Mewtwo, Green, and the Mega Stones you were missing
body: Cerulean Cave sits on the north-west edge of Cerulean City, behind water. Sea Skim across, or fly over it. The Coach Trainer who was blocking the entrance has moved aside and can now be fought — he hands over TM60 Megahorn.

Throw the Master Ball at Mewtwo. Not at the birds, which never flee and can be worn down with Golden Razz Berries all afternoon; not at a Snorlax; at Mewtwo. It is level 70 with all stats boosted, and while it also never flees, it has the worst catch rate in the game and it will eat a very large number of Ultra Balls. You have been carrying the ball since stage 11 for exactly this.

body.where: Cerulean Cave B1F — the south-west island, via Sea Skim
body.why: Level 70, all stats boosted, at least three perfect IVs, and it never flees. 154 Special Attack and 130 Speed. Two Mega forms once Green gives you the stones. It respawns if you defeat it or run, so it is not missable — it is only expensive.

body.where: Cerulean Cave 2F — common here rather than rare
body.why: This is the best place in the game to farm Chansey. On 2F it is an ordinary spawn rather than a rare one, and Chansey is the richest experience and Candy payout in Kanto. Chain it.

body.where: Cerulean Cave — all floors
body.why: The second of Ditto’s two homes, and much denser than the Pokémon Mansion. If you left Cinnabar without one, fix it here.

body.where: Cerulean Cave — all floors
body.why: Cerulean Cave is the only place Lickitung exists in this game. No trade, no route spawn. If you want the Pokédex it is here or nowhere.

body.why: Fully evolved and wild. Poliwhirl needs a Water Stone otherwise, and Politoed does not exist here.

body.where: Cerulean Cave — common
body.why: Denser than Victory Road, and at a higher level.

body: The glowing crystal spots on 2F and B1F respawn fossils. Every 256 steps the game re-rolls the hidden items on a floor — you have to leave and re-enter for it to take effect — and the spot beside Mewtwo’s island refreshes at midnight and is guaranteed to hold a fossil, with roughly 40% each for the Dome and Helix Fossils and 20% for the Old Amber. This is how you get the fossil you refused at Mt. Moon, and it is why that choice was never permanent.

body.name: Mewtwo

team.note: All stats boosted on top of 154 Special Attack, 130 Speed and 106 HP. It carries Recover and will undo your progress if you go slowly.

plan: Save first. Five-minute timer, and this is the longest interactive battle in the game.
Bug, Ghost and Dark are the only types that hurt it. X-Scissor from Route 12, Shadow Ball from TM43, Dark Pulse from the Rocket Hideout, or Foul Play from the Pokémon Mansion.
Recover is the problem, not the damage. Paralyse it with TM16 Thunder Wave or your partner’s Splishy Splash, or put it to sleep — a Parasect’s Spore never misses — and it stops out-healing you.
It outspeeds almost everything you own at 130 base Speed. Your partner’s Zippy Zap at +2 priority is one of the very few moves that reliably lands first.
Then throw the Master Ball. Mewtwo never flees, so you could grind Ultra Balls instead — but this is the one target in the game where the guaranteed catch is worth more than the balls.
body.reward: A level-70 Mewtwo with at least three perfect IVs, and the strongest Pokémon in the game by a wide margin.

body.name: Green

team.note: Moonblast, Light Screen, Reflect, Tri Attack. Both screens go up — Brick Break removes them.
Dark Pulse, Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Will-O-Wisp. Normal and Fighting do nothing to it.
Power Whip, Poison Jab, Sucker Punch, Leech Life. Sucker Punch has priority and it is Dark.
Fire Blast, Dark Pulse, Foul Play, Hyper Beam. Foul Play uses your Attack against you — do not send a physical monster at it.
Dizzy Punch, Sucker Punch, Thunder Punch, Brick Break. Four physical moves and no way to hit a Ghost.
Hydro Pump, Flash Cannon, Ice Beam, Fake Out. Fake Out flinches you the turn it comes in.

plan: She turns up on Mewtwo’s island after you have caught it, and only after you leave the cave, meet Trace and come back. If she is not there, you have skipped a step.
Electric and Grass split her team in half — Blastoise takes 2× from both, and your partner’s Zippy Zap or Splishy Splash covers the Ninetales and the Kangaskhan.
Ground answers the Ninetales, and Psychic answers the Victreebel and Gengar. Note that Gengar is immune to Normal and Fighting entirely.
Do not lead a heavy physical attacker into the Ninetales — Foul Play calculates off the target’s Attack, so the harder your Pokémon hits, the harder it gets hit.
Clefable is pure Fairy: Steel and Poison are 2× on it, and it is immune to Dragon.

stages.title: The rematch circuit, the Mega Stone merchant, and the last Rockets
body: The Poké Maniac by the Indigo Plateau Poké Mart sells the Mega Stones you were never given. Blue handed you the four starter stones and Green handed you the two Mewtwonites; this man sells the rest — Beedrillite, Pidgeotite, Alakazite, Slowbronite, Gengarite, Kangaskhanite, Pinsirite, Gyaradosite and Aerodactylite, plus spares of the ones you have. They are expensive, so run the daily gym rematches for the money. Buy Aerodactylite first: Mega Aerodactyl goes to 135 Attack and 150 Speed, and your Aerodactyl came free from a fossil you nearly forgot in Pewter.

Mega Evolution in this game has no held-item cost. The stone sits in your Bag and the Mega button appears for any Pokémon of that species. You still get one Mega per battle, and it reverts when the battle ends. Thirteen species can Mega Evolve here — the three Kanto starters, Beedrill, Pidgeot, Alakazam, Slowbro, Gengar, Kangaskhan, Pinsir, Gyarados, Aerodactyl and Mewtwo — and Charizard and Mewtwo have two forms each.

Pinsir is a Let’s Go, Eevee exclusive, so on Let’s Go, Pikachu! the Pinsirite is a stone with nothing to put it on unless you trade for one. Your side of that swap is Scyther, from Routes 14 and 15. If you have a trading partner, do both at once.

Every Gym Leader can be re-battled once a day, and all eight bring a five-Pokémon team at level 56 to 57 — considerably harder than their gym rosters. Blue holds the Viridian Gym now with a six at level 66 to 68. The Elite Four also come back, at 61 to 65, with Trace at 66 to 67.

plan: He is the leader of the Coach Trainers and he is on the third floor of the Celadon Condominiums, in the Game Freak office. He does not gate anything — he is here for the fight.

body: The Shiny Charm is the real prize on this floor. Complete the Pokédex — 150 species, with the usual exceptions — and the Game Freak director gives you a Diploma and the Charm, which raises wild shiny odds permanently. Stacked with a Catch Combo of 31 or more and a Lure, it takes the rate from 1 in 4096 to 15 in 4096, which is roughly one in 273. That is the difference between shiny hunting being feasible and not.

stages.title: Filling the last gaps in the Pokédex
body: The Game Freak director in the Celadon Condominiums wants 150 recorded species. Kanto gives you 136 of them on your own cartridge. The rest are below.
Trade evolutions — four species, and no way round them

Let’s Go kept trade evolutions and gave you nothing to replace them with. There is no Linking Cord, no Everstone workaround and no in-game NPC that will do the swap for you. Machamp, Golem, Gengar and Alakazam each require you to trade a Machoke, Graveler, Haunter or Kadabra to a second player and have them trade it back. Line all four up in one session — the evolution triggers on the trade itself, so you get them back already evolved.

These eleven exist only in Let’s Go, Eevee!. There is no wild spawn, gift or in-game trade for any of them on your cartridge — they come from a trade with an Eevee player, or from Pokémon GO through the GO Park. In exchange, the Eevee player needs Oddish, Gloom, Vileplume, Sandshrew, Sandslash, Mankey, Primeape, Growlithe, Grimer, Muk and Scyther from you, so a single swap session closes both dexes.

rows: Every Poké Ball Plus accessory ships with a Mew inside. Connect it once and take the Mew; each accessory gives exactly one, and it cannot be extracted twice.

stages.title: Catch Combos — the mechanic the whole game is built on
body: Catch two or more of the same species in a row and the game starts counting a Catch Combo in the top-left of the encounter screen. Keep catching that species and the counter climbs; catch anything else, or let one flee, and it resets.
What breaks a chain, and what does not
Breaks it: a wild Pokémon fleeing from you.
Breaks it: catching a different species — including another member of the same evolutionary line. A Pidgeotto does not continue a Pidgey chain.
Does not break it: running away from an encounter yourself. Missing balls, fleeing on purpose, walking away — all free.
Does not break it: changing route or entering a city. The chain and its effects travel with you.
Does not break it: catching in the GO Park, which counts towards the chain but gets none of the benefits.

A long chain makes wild Pokémon more likely to run. The base flee value drops by twice the chain length, so at a combo of 60 things bolt noticeably faster. That is the trade: better spawns, jumpier targets. Use Razz Berries to hold them still, and remember that a flee is the one thing that ends the chain.

Chain the commonest thing on the route to force the rarest. Rare spawns — Bulbasaur in Viridian Forest, Charmander on Routes 3, 4 and Rock Tunnel, Squirtle on Routes 24, 25 and Seafoam, Lapras on Routes 19 and 20, Chansey almost everywhere — sit at roughly 1% with no chain and 50% at a chain of 31 or more. The correct way to hunt a Lapras is not to wander Route 19 hoping; it is to catch thirty-one Tentacool and then look up.

For a competitive-quality Pokémon, chain to 31 and then catch the thing you actually want. At 31+ every catch has four guaranteed perfect IVs. Combine that with 200 Awakening Values fed by Candy and maxed friendship, and a wild Pokémon out of a long chain is stronger than anything the story hands you.

For shinies, the chain must stay live. The boosted shiny rate applies only to the next member of the chained species to spawn — so a player who reaches 31 and then stands still is back to base odds. Keep catching. At a chain of 31+ with a Lure and the Shiny Charm the rate is 15 in 4096, about one in 273, against a base of one in 4096.

Cerulean Cave 2F is the best chaining ground in the game. Chansey is an ordinary spawn there rather than a rare one, it pays the most experience and Candy of anything in Kanto, and the floor is a single open chamber — so you can chain it to 31 and beyond without walking anywhere.

stages.place: How Let’s Go differs from every other Kanto game
stages.title: The rules that decide every recommendation in this guide
body: 1. Damage class belongs to the move, not the type

In Generation III a Fire move was special because Fire was a special type, full stop. That rule was abolished in Generation IV and Let’s Go is Generation VII, so every move carries its own damage class. Flare Blitz is a physical Fire move; Flamethrower is a special one. Vine Whip and Razor Leaf are physical Grass moves, which is why Venusaur — 82 Attack, 100 Special Attack — wants Mega Drain, Sludge Bomb and Solar Beam from TMs rather than the Grass moves it learns by levelling. Check the class of a move against the stat of the Pokémon holding it, every time.
2. Fairy exists, and Kanto is full of it

Fairy was introduced in Generation VI and it is here. Clefairy and Clefable are pure Fairy — not Normal. Jigglypuff, Wigglytuff and Mr. Mime are part Fairy. Fairy is 2× into Dragon, Dark and Fighting, is completely immune to Dragon, and is walled by Steel, Fire and Poison. A Clefable takes Lance’s Dragonite’s Outrage for zero damage — something no Pokémon in the original Kanto could do. In the other direction, Steel no longer resists Ghost or Dark: that resistance was removed in Generation VI, so a Magneton does not wall Agatha’s Shadow Balls.
3. No Abilities, no held items, no breeding, no weather, no day and night

Let’s Go strips out almost every system layered onto Kanto since Generation II. There are no Abilities — Lightning Rod, Levitate and Intimidate simply do not exist, so type charts read literally. There are no held items, so Mega Stones live in the Bag and Leftovers, berries in battle and Choice items are all absent. There is no breeding, no Day Care and no Eggs. There is no weather and no day/night cycle, so nothing in the game is time-gated except a handful of daily item respawns.
4. EVs are gone; Awakening Values replace them
5. Wild Pokémon are caught, not fought

Wild Pokémon stand in the overworld and are caught with a ball throw. There is no wild-battle experience — catching is how you level, and a Catch Combo multiplies that by up to ×3. The exceptions are the interactive Pokémon: both Snorlax, the item-shaped Electrode in the Power Plant, and every legendary. Those must be battled and knocked out first, on a five-minute timer that does not pause for the HOME button, with boosted stats — Snorlax gets an Attack or Defense lift, legendaries get all six — and whatever you catch is guaranteed at least three perfect IVs.
7. The Pokémon Box is in your Bag

There is no PC and no Bill’s system. The Box opens from the Bag anywhere in the world, including mid-route, and moving Pokémon in and out is free. Keeping a party slot open is pointless: with six in the party every catch, gift and revived fossil goes to the Box automatically. Any guide that tells you to deposit something before a gift is describing a different game.
8. Badges buy obedience and nothing else

No stat boosts — that was Generation I. Obedience is set by how many badges you hold, not which: 1 → level 20, 2 → 30, 3 → 40, 4 → 50, 5 → 60, 6 → 70, 7 → 80, 8 → unlimited. It applies only to Pokémon you did not catch yourself. Several gyms have their own entry requirements instead, listed in the table below.

body: The set: Zippy Zap, Floaty Fall, Splishy Splash and Brick Break. Zippy Zap is your Electric STAB and it is better than Thunderbolt for a Pokémon this fast; Floaty Fall and Splishy Splash cover the two halves of the type chart Electric cannot reach, and they run off different attacking stats so no single wall stops all three. TM13 Brick Break from Route 10 is the fourth: 75 power Fighting, and it destroys Reflect and Light Screen on contact — which is Sabrina’s entire gym, Green’s Clefable and Trace’s Slowbro.

Pika Papow is a partner power, not a move slot. Once your partner’s friendship is high enough an icon appears in battle; trigger it and it uses Pika Papow, which never misses and whose power is friendship ÷ 2.5, topping out at 102 at maximum friendship. Trigger it while your partner is not the active Pokémon and it boosts the stats of whoever is instead. Feed Candy, play with it, and let it walk beside you — high friendship also gives every Pokémon in the party up to a 10% boost to all stats.

None of the five occupies a move slot and none of them is used in battle — they are field actions on the “Play with Pikachu” menu. That is a straight upgrade over HMs, and it means your partner carries four real attacks all game. After the Hall of Fame, riding Charizard, Aerodactyl or Dragonite through the sky bypasses every Chop Down and Sea Skim obstacle, so the techniques become optional shortcuts rather than requirements.

stages.title: Team planner
Where this came from, and how to keep your ticks
body: Encounter tables, learnsets, TM-to-move mapping, base stats and typings come from PokéAPI, filtered to version group lets-go-pikachu-lets-go-eevee and version lets-go-pikachu. Spawn rates, trainer parties, item placements, walkthrough ordering, Master Trainer levels and every game-mechanic description come from Bulbapedia raw wikitext via the MediaWiki API. Every Gym Leader, Elite Four member and rival team was cross-checked against at least two Bulbapedia pages — the trainer’s own article and the gym or Indigo Plateau article — and the two agree throughout.

Where PokéAPI and Bulbapedia disagree, this guide follows Bulbapedia. PokéAPI does not carry Let’s Go’s move-power overrides: it reports Mega Drain at 40 when this game uses 75, Solar Beam at 120 when this game uses 200, Sky Attack at 140 when this game uses 200, and Absorb at 20 when this game uses 40. It also reports the Generation VIII rewrites of Zippy Zap, Splishy Splash and Floaty Fall rather than the Let’s Go originals. Those eight moves are corrected by hand from the Bulbapedia move pages; every other number in the TM index is PokéAPI’s.

PokéAPI also does not publish Let’s Go spawn rates — its encounter rows all report 100 — so every percentage in this guide comes from Bulbapedia’s walkthrough tables, and the two sources were reconciled against each other to catch anything either had missed.

This guide is written for Let’s Go, Pikachu! specifically. Where the two versions differ — exclusive Pokémon, the Vermilion gift, the Celadon and Cinnabar trade counters, and Trace’s final team — it describes your side and names theirs.

Play Rough at 35 — Fairy, 90 power, and 2× into Dark, Dragon and Fighting. Also put TM20 Dark Pulse on it: 80 power special Dark off a 100 Special Attack is your answer to Sabrina.
Earthquake at 36. The moment it lands, let it become Sandslash.
Nothing due. Erika’s gym is a bad room for it — Vileplume’s Moonblast is Fairy.

mv.why: 90 power physical Flying with a 30% flinch, and 2× into Grass, Fighting and Bug. The second of your partner’s three exclusive moves.
75 power in Let’s Go, special, and it heals half the damage dealt — functionally Giga Drain. Ivysaur’s 80 Special Attack is the stat this move uses; Razor Leaf is physical and uses the wrong one.
80 power special Dark off a 100 Special Attack. Kanto gives you almost no Dark, and this is the move that makes Sabrina straightforward.
100 power, perfect accuracy, and the payoff for fourteen levels of holding B. Evolve it into Sandslash immediately afterwards.

k09.now: Learn Floaty Fall, beat Erika, clear the Rocket Hideout for the Silph Scope, and take Sky Dash from the Rocker outside the Game Corner.

k10.sum: Pokémon Tower. Jessie and James are both Poison, so this is a Psychic and Ground room — leave your partner and your Fire types out of it.

slots.w: Evolved at 32, and it gains Petal Dance free on evolving — 120 power special Grass, which is exactly the stat Venusaur has. Unlike Growlithe, evolve this one the moment it is offered.
Earthquake is on it and it is 2× into both Arbok and Weezing. This is the fight it walks.
Nothing useful in the tower — Ghost resists nothing you carry and both Rockets are Poison. Bench it for the top floor.
Charizard at 36. Watch for it and let it happen — Heat Wave and Wing Attack arrive with the evolution.
Flare Blitz at 38. Two levels away from the Fire Stone.
Fighting does nothing at all to a Ghost. Gastly and Haunter are immune. Keep it out of the tower floors.

k10.now: Climb Pokémon Tower with the Silph Scope and walk Mr. Fuji home for the Poké Flute.

k11.sum: Eleven floors of Silph Co. is what gets you to the level-45 bar on Sabrina’s door. The team does not change, but Growlithe finally becomes Arcanine and Charizard arrives.

slots.w: Evolved at 36 with Heat Wave and Wing Attack free. Put TM37 Flamethrower on it from Silph Co. 10F — Charizard does not learn it until level 54 otherwise.
Use the Fire Stone now, once Flare Blitz is in at 38. Lead it against Sabrina: Dark Pulse is 2× into three of her four, off a 100 Special Attack, and its 95 Speed outruns everything except Alakazam.
Zippy Zap removes Alakazam. 55 HP and 45 Defense behind 120 Speed — a guaranteed crit at +2 priority is exactly the answer to a glass cannon. Brick Break clears Mr. Mime’s screens.
Keep it out of the Saffron Gym. Poison takes 2× from Psychic and Venusaur is half Poison.
Earthquake. Neutral into everything Sabrina owns, which is more than most of your team manages.
Psychic resists Fighting, so it is a poor fit here too. Snorlax takes this slot on Route 16.

mv.why: 90 power against 40, same type, same class. Charizard’s own learnset does not offer it until level 54.
Flare Blitz landed at 38. Everything Growlithe had to learn, it has learnt — Arcanine’s own level-up list adds nothing.
90 power special Poison, in the Pokémon Mansion four stages from now. Keep a slot free for it — Venusaur is a special attacker with no special STAB besides Petal Dance and Mega Drain.

k11.now: Clear all eleven floors of Silph Co. for the Master Ball and the levels you need to get past Sabrina’s level-45 door check.

k12.sum: Snorlax takes Primeape’s slot. 160 HP, 110 Attack, no weakness except Fighting — it is the body that survives the fights your glass cannons lose.

slots.w: Wake the Route 16 one with the Poké Flute and knock it out before you throw. It arrives around level 34 with at least three perfect IVs, learns Body Slam at 52 and Crunch at 58, and takes TM41 Earthquake off Giovanni later.

Take Splishy Splash from the Fuchsia Move Tutor. Water, special, 90 power, 30% paralysis — and it covers Ground and Rock, which are the only things that threaten your partner. The set is now complete.
Ground is 2× into three of Koga’s four. Only the Golbat escapes it, and that is what your partner is for.
Nothing due. Dark Pulse and Flare Blitz are its two best moves and both are on it.
Air Slash at 62 is a long way off — Wing Attack is the Flying move it uses until then.
Poison-type Venusaur is immune to Toxic, which is the move Koga’s entire gym is built around. Bring it.

mv.why: 90 power special Water with a 30% paralysis chance. Your partner now covers Electric, Flying and Water off two different attack stats, plus Brick Break — nothing in Kanto walls all four.
That is roughly the set a level-34 Snorlax arrives with, so plan from there. Keep Rest — a full heal for two sleeping turns on 160 HP is a genuine reset button.
85 power against Headbutt’s 70, with a 30% paralysis chance. Yawn is the dead slot.

k12.now: Wake the Route 16 Snorlax and catch it, learn Splishy Splash in Fuchsia, take Sea Skim in the Playful Park, then beat Koga.

k13.sum: A collecting loop rather than a fighting one. No changes to the six — but TM32 Dazzling Gleam is on Route 12 and it is the only Fairy move in the game.

slots.w: Catch the second Snorlax on Route 12 as well and box it — its Master Trainer is a level-75 fight later.
Complete set. Nothing further to learn.
Nothing due.
Nothing due.
Nothing due.
Lapras takes this slot on Route 19. Box Sandslash rather than releasing it — it is a Master Trainer species and a Let’s Go, Pikachu! exclusive.

mv.why: 80 power special Fairy — the only Fairy TM in the game. Snorlax has 65 Special Attack, so this is a coverage move rather than a damage move, but Fairy is 2× into Dragon, Dark and Fighting and nothing else on your team carries it.

k13.now: Catch the second Snorlax, take TM32 Dazzling Gleam from Mr. Dazzling, and trade the Route 19 Gold Teeth to the warden for Strong Push.

k14.sum: Lapras completes the six. Water/Ice with 130 HP answers Lance, Giovanni and Blaine, and it doubles as your Sea Skim mount.

slots.w: A rare spawn on the water of Routes 19 and 20 — chain Tentacool at 30% to force it. It learns Ice Beam at 39 and Surf at 45 without help, and Ice is 4× into Dragonite.
Zippy Zap is the right move for Articuno. Electric is 2×, the crit is predictable, and +2 priority means you always land the last hit before it acts. Rock would be 4× and kill it.
Fire is 2× on Articuno as well, if you want a second option.
Keep it away from Articuno. Snorlax will be carrying Rock Slide by now and Rock is 4× on Ice/Flying — it will kill the thing you came to catch.
Grass is resisted by Ice and Flying both. Nothing to do in the Seafoam Islands.
Fire is 2× on Articuno, but Charizard is 4× weak to its Rock coverage and 2× to Ice. Do not lead it.

mv.why: 90 power special Ice, learnt for free. It is 4× into Lance’s Dragonite and 2× into half the Elite Four.
90 power against 40, same type and class. TM47 Surf from Route 15 covers you if you would rather not wait.
Lapras learns Ice Beam by itself at 39. Put the machine on Blastoise or Starmie instead.

k14.now: Chain Tentacool on Route 19 until a Lapras appears, then push the Seafoam boulders into the sea and catch Articuno — with Electric or Fire, never Rock.

k15.sum: Cinnabar is a Water fight. Lead Lapras, carry Burn Heals, and pick up the Sludge Bomb that Venusaur has been keeping a slot open for.

slots.w: Water is 2× into all four of Blaine’s, Water/Ice resists Fire back, and 130 HP absorbs a Fire Blast without complaint.

TM52 Sludge Bomb is in the Pokémon Mansion basement. 90 power special Poison, and it is the same-type special move Venusaur’s 100 Special Attack has been waiting for. Keep it out of the gym itself — Fire is 2× on Grass.
Body Slam at 52. Rock Slide from the mansion is worth a slot too — but remember it is 4× on all three legendary birds.
Resists Fire, so it survives the gym comfortably — it just cannot hurt anything in it.
Same problem. Bench both Fire types for Blaine.
Electric is neutral on every Fire type. Splishy Splash is the move to use here.

mv.why: 90 power special Poison. Between this, Mega Drain and Petal Dance, Venusaur finally has three special moves that match its 100 Special Attack.
75 power physical Rock with a flinch chance. Note it and remember it — Rock is 4× on Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres, so Snorlax must sit out all three legendary catches.

k15.now: Revive all three fossils at the Cinnabar Lab, clear the Mansion for the Secret Key and TM52, then beat Blaine with Lapras.

k16.sum: Zapdos, then the Mega Stones. Lapras carries the catch; Charizard carries the rest of the game once you pick a stone.

slots.w: Ice Beam, not Rock. Electric/Flying is 4× weak to Rock and will die to it. Ice is 2× and gives you the controlled damage a catch needs.

Blue’s Charizardite Y is the stone to use. Mega Charizard Y takes 109 Special Attack to 159 and keeps Fire/Flying, which is what Flamethrower and Fire Blast want. X trades the Flying half for Dragon and pushes Attack instead — the wrong stat for this Charizard.
Rock Slide again. Keep it out of the Zapdos fight.
Grass is resisted by Electric and Flying both — nothing to do against Zapdos. The Venusaurite is the fallback if you would rather have a wall than a cannon.
Nothing due.
Electric on Electric is resisted. Splishy Splash is neutral; Floaty Fall is resisted. This is Lapras’ fight.

k16.now: Catch Zapdos at the Power Plant with Ice Beam, then take the Key Stone and four Mega Stones from Blue at Oak’s lab.

k17.sum: Giovanni is a Water and Grass fight, and the TM he drops is the best physical machine in the game. Put it on Snorlax.

slots.w: Surf is 2× into all four and 4× into Rhydon, and Lapras’ 130 HP absorbs an Earthquake.
Grass is 4× on Rhydon and 2× on the rest, and being part Poison it takes Nidoking’s Poison Jab at half. Mega Venusaur if you want it boring.
TM41 Earthquake goes here. 100 power off 110 Attack, and it plugs every hole a pure Normal movepool has — Electric, Rock, Steel, Fire and Poison all take 2×.
Immune to Earthquake, which is the move on four of Giovanni’s Pokémon. A safe switch-in even without a super-effective move.
Nothing due. Fire is neutral into Ground.
Electric is a straight zero into three of the four. Splishy Splash is the only move it should use in this gym.

mv.why: 100 power, perfect accuracy, and it is 2× into five types. Sandslash and Dugtrio learn it by level-up, so this is the one Pokémon on your team the machine is worth spending on — and dropping Rock Slide also stops Snorlax overkilling Moltres two stages from now.

k17.now: Beat Giovanni at the Viridian Gym and put TM41 Earthquake on Snorlax.

k18.sum: Victory Road, then Moltres. Everything is in place — this stage is levelling and one more careful legendary catch.

slots.w: Surf, not Rock Slide. Fire/Flying is 4× weak to Rock and a level-60 physical attacker will kill it outright. Water is 2× and controllable.
Earthquake does nothing to a Flying type and Rock Slide would kill it. Leave Snorlax out of the Moltres fight entirely.
Splishy Splash is 2× on Moltres and the 30% paralysis makes the throwing phase easier.
TM45 Solar Beam is in this cave. 200 power in Let’s Go — not the 120 it is elsewhere — and on 100 Special Attack it is the biggest hit your team owns.
Nothing due. Save the Mega for the League.
Fire is resisted by Fire. Nothing to do against Moltres.

mv.why: 200 power in this game. It spends a turn charging, which is a real cost — but Petal Dance locks you in for 2–3 turns and confuses you afterwards, so this is a straight upgrade on a Pokémon bulky enough to survive the charge.
110 power at 70% accuracy against Ice Beam’s 90 at 100%. In a five-battle gauntlet with no healing between rounds, the reliable one wins.

k18.now: Sweep Victory Road’s TMs, Sea Skim every Route 23 island for Golden Razz Berries, and catch Moltres with Water — keep Snorlax and its Rock Slide away from it.

k19.sum: The final six. Five battles with no Pokémon Center between them — buy twenty Full Restores, use Madame Memorial to fix any move you regret, and spend your one Mega on Charizard Y in the Champion’s room.

slots.w: The best Pokémon on your team for two of the five rooms. Electric is 2× into four of Lorelei’s five, and Lance’s Aerodactyl and Gyarados are both 4×. Zippy Zap’s guaranteed crit at +2 priority removes them before they move.
Ice Beam is 4× into Dragonite and 2× into half of Bruno. 130 HP is what carries you through a gauntlet with no healing station.
Earthquake is 2× into four of Agatha’s five — every one of them is part Poison. Body Slam does nothing at all to either Gengar, so Earthquake is the move you use in that room.
Flying is 2× into four of Bruno’s five. Mega Evolve in the Champion’s room — 159 Special Attack, and Heat Wave answers Trace’s Vileplume, Pidgeot and Marowak.
Grass is 4× on Bruno’s Onix and 2× on Poliwrath, Cloyster and Slowbro. Keep it away from Trace’s Pidgeot and Rapidash.
Dark Pulse is 2× into both Gengar; Flare Blitz answers Bruno’s Onix and Trace’s Vileplume. 95 Speed outruns most of the gauntlet.

mv.why: Zippy Zap, Splishy Splash, Floaty Fall and Brick Break. If any of the three tutor moves is missing, the tutors in Cerulean, Celadon and Fuchsia will re-teach them free.
One Heart Scale. Body Slam at 52 and Crunch at 58 are both worth having, and the Cerulean bike shop gave you five scales.
One Mega Evolution per battle, and it wears off when the battle ends. Spend it in the Champion’s room, not on Lorelei.

k19.now: Buy twenty Full Restores, visit Madame Memorial with your Heart Scales, then start the gauntlet and save your one Mega for Trace.

p01.sum: Master Trainer battles are one-versus-one with a species match and no items, so your carefully built six is irrelevant for them — what matters is having a strong specimen of the right species. Your six is still the team you take to Red.

slots.w: Red’s own Pikachu is level 85 with Reflect. Your partner has a partner’s stats and Zippy Zap; his does not.
Also your ride. Set it as your buddy and take to the sky — that is where Dragonite, Pidgeot and eventually the three birds live.
Red brings his own Lapras at 85 with an entirely physical moveset.
Red’s Snorlax runs Toxic, Protect and Rest and will stall you out if you let it. Remove it early.
Red’s Venusaur is the Mega, and it is his last Pokémon. Amnesia plus Leech Seed is the shape of that fight.
Red brings one too, with Roar — which will drag your lead out and pick its replacement for you.

p01.now: Set a Charizard as your buddy and take to the sky, then beat six Master Trainers to make Red appear at the Indigo Plateau.

p02.sum: Mewtwo is a five-minute battle against a level-70 Psychic with Recover and 130 Speed. Status first, damage second, Master Ball third.

slots.w: Zippy Zap is one of the very few moves that reliably moves before Mewtwo. +2 priority beats 130 base Speed. Splishy Splash’s 30% paralysis is the other reason to bring it.
Dark is 2× into Psychic and Snorlax learns Crunch at 58. 160 HP also means it survives a boosted Psychic, which most of your team will not.
Dark Pulse off a 100 Special Attack. Along with Snorlax’s Crunch this is most of the damage you have that Mewtwo does not resist.
Neutral, but 159 Special Attack as Mega Y is raw damage that gets through anything.
Neutral into Psychic and bulky enough to eat a hit while you set up paralysis.
Bring it for one reason: Sleep Powder. A sleeping Mewtwo cannot use Recover, which is the only thing that actually beats you here. Parasect’s Spore never misses if you would rather be certain.

p02.now: Clear Cerulean Cave, throw the Master Ball at Mewtwo, then leave, talk to Trace, come back and beat Green for the Mewtwonites.
